Two integrations by parts move the derivatives onto the fields, and only $\nabla\cdot\bE$ survives. Gauss's law, including the ionic bound charge,

$$\nabla\cdot\bE=4\pi\big(\rho_{\rm e}+\rho_{\rm ion}\big),\qquad\rho_{\rm ion}=-\nabla\cdot\bP, \tag{E.234}$$

then gives the central result of EPP §4.4:

$$\boxed{H^0_{\rm Lph}=\frac12\int d\br\int d\br'\,\frac{\big[\rho_{\rm e}(\br)+\rho_{\rm ion}(\br)\big]\big[\rho_{\rm e}(\br')+\rho_{\rm ion}(\br')\big]}{|\br-\br'|}} \tag{E.235}$$
Derivation: from (E.227) to (E.235)

Because $\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu e^{-\ii\bq\cdot(\br-\br')}=q_\mu q_\nu e^{-\ii\bq\cdot(\br-\br')}$, with $\partial'_\nu=\partial/\partial x'_\nu$, the kernel can be written with the Coulomb propagator:

$$H^0_{\rm Lph}=\frac{1}{32\pi^2}\int d\br\int d\br'\sum_{\mu\nu}E_\mu(\br)\left\{\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu\int\frac{d\bq}{(2\pi)^3}\frac{4\pi}{q^2}e^{-\ii\bq\cdot(\br-\br')}\right\}E_\nu(\br'), \tag{E.228}$$ $$\int\frac{d\bq}{(2\pi)^3}\frac{4\pi}{q^2}e^{-\ii\bq\cdot(\br-\br')}=V(\br-\br')=\frac{1}{|\br-\br'|}. \tag{E.229}$$

With the derivatives acting only on $V$,

$$H^0_{\rm Lph}=\frac{1}{32\pi^2}\int d\br\,\bE(\br)\cdot\nabla_{\br}\int d\br'\,\big\{\nabla_{\br'}V(\br-\br')\big\}\cdot\bE(\br'). \tag{E.231}$$

Integrating by parts in $\br'$ (the surface term vanishes) turns the inner integral into $-\int d\br'\,V(\br-\br')\,\nabla_{\br'}\cdot\bE(\br')$, which is (E.232). The same step in $\br$ gives

$$H^0_{\rm Lph}=\frac{1}{32\pi^2}\int d\br\,\big[\nabla_{\br}\cdot\bE(\br)\big]\int d\br'\,V(\br-\br')\,\big[\nabla_{\br'}\cdot\bE(\br')\big]. \tag{E.233}$$

The transverse part of $\bE$ has dropped out, as it must. Inserting (E.234) gives the prefactor $(4\pi)^2/32\pi^2=\frac12$ of (E.235).

The same identity is quick to check in Fourier space, with the normalization of (E.190). Gauss's law gives $\tilde E_{3\bq}=-4\pi\ii\rho_\bq/q$, so that, with $v(q)=4\pi/q^2$,

$$\frac{1}{8\pi}\sum_\bq|\tilde E_{3\bq}|^2=\sum_\bq\frac{2\pi|\rho_\bq|^2}{q^2}=\frac12\sum_\bq v(q)\,|\rho_\bq|^2 .$$

The energy of the longitudinal field is exactly the instantaneous Coulomb energy of all charges. No Coulomb term was put into the Lagrangian; it was hidden in $\frac{1}{8\pi}\int E^2$ all along. "Instantaneous" is literal: $\bE_l$ has no equation of motion of its own, so at each time it is fixed by the charges at that time. Expanding the square of (E.235) gives three interactions, each of which Part B will dress:

  • Electron–electron, $\frac12\iint\rho_{\rm e}\rho_{\rm e}'/|\br-\br'|$: the bare Coulomb interaction. RPA dressing turns it into $W^{\rm e}$.
  • Electron–ion, $\iint\rho_{\rm e}\rho_{\rm ion}'/|\br-\br'|$: the energy of an electron in the field of the ionic dipoles. After phonon quantization this is the bare (unscreened, $\epsilon^\infty\to1$) Fröhlich vertex $\propto\ii\,\bq\cdot\hat Z^*_a\be_{a\sigma}/q^2$ ($\be_{a\sigma}$: phonon eigenvector). The factor that turns $q^2$ into $\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^\infty\cdot\bq$ is not inserted by hand: it is generated by $\Pi^{\rm e}$ (§B.8, §B.9).
  • Ion–ion, $\frac12\iint\rho_{\rm ion}\rho_{\rm ion}'/|\br-\br'|$: the dipole–dipole interaction. At long wavelength $\bE_l=-4\pi\bP_\parallel$, which stiffens only the longitudinal optical mode by $\Delta\omega^2=\omega_p^2=4\pi Z^{*2}/(\Omega_{\rm uc}M)$, the unscreened LO shift of §B.3. For GaAs this unscreened shift would put the LO phonon near 56 meV instead of the measured 36 meV; dividing $\omega_p^2$ by $\epsilon^\infty=10.9$ restores 36 meV (numbers in §B.7). TO modes carry no bound charge and couple only to transverse photons, which is where polaritons come from (§B.6).

Link to Giustino: the Coulomb Hamiltonian, derived

Giustino §IV.A starts from $\hat H=\hat T_{\rm e}+\hat T_{\rm n}+\hat U_{\rm ee}+\hat U_{\rm nn}+\hat U_{\rm en}$ (G Eqs. 62–67), every interaction being the postulated instantaneous $v(\br,\br')$, with no vector potential (§A.5). (E.235) is that structure, obtained as the longitudinal sector of electrodynamics. Two differences matter. EPP's ions enter only through the induced dipole density $-\nabla\cdot\bP$ with Born charges; the linear term of Giustino's nuclear density expansion (G Eq. 107), $Z_\kappa\Delta\boldsymbol\tau_{\kappa p}\cdot\nabla\delta(\br-\boldsymbol\tau^0_{\kappa p})$, is the same point-dipole density with bare charges $Z_\kappa$, and the static lattice charge stays in $V_{\rm cr}$. And (E.235) keeps the self-interaction terms that G Eq. 64 removes with $-\delta(\br-\br')$ and G Eq. 65 excludes; normal ordering of the electron term and dropping on-site dipole terms, neither mentioned by EPP, must remove them. For the RPA/BSE practitioner: the bare $v$ in $W=v+v\chi v$ is the electron–electron part of $H^0_{\rm Lph}$, and the transverse photons of (E.214) are what a Coulomb-only theory leaves out.

Note on the source: number density or charge density

EPP defines $\rho_{\rm e}=\Psi^\dagger\Psi$ (E.239), a number density, and calls it the "electronic charge density operator" before (E.235). Gauss's law (E.234), the Coulomb energy (E.235) and the last term of (E.237) need the charge density $e\Psi^\dagger\Psi$, which is also what $\rho_{\rm e}$ means in (E.179)–(E.180) by continuity with (E.166). On this page $\rho_{\rm e}=e\Psi^\dagger\Psi$ in all Coulomb terms. In the diamagnetic $A^2$ term of (E.237) the number density is correct, and we write it explicitly as $\Psi^\dagger\Psi$. The same slip recurs in the total interaction (E.312) of §B.6.

The final split: $H_0$ and $V'$

Moving the Coulomb term out of $H_0'$ and into the interaction, $H_0=H_0'-H^0_{\rm Lph}$ and $V'=V+H^0_{\rm Lph}$ (EPP §4.4.4), leaves a genuinely free Hamiltonian of Kohn–Sham electrons, bare phonons and transverse photons,

$$\begin{aligned}H_0={}&\sum_n\sum_{\bk\in{\rm BZ}}E_{n\bk}\,c^\dagger_{n\bk}c_{n\bk}+\sum_{\alpha=1}^{3s}\sum_{\bq\in{\rm BZ}}\hbar\omega_\alpha(\bq)\Big(a^\dagger_{\bq\alpha}a_{\bq\alpha}+\frac12\Big)\\&+\sum_{\bq,\sigma=1,2}\hbar qc\,\Big\{b^\dagger_{\bq\sigma}b_{\bq\sigma}+\frac12\Big\},\end{aligned} \tag{E.236}$$

and an interaction that contains every coupling:

$$\begin{aligned}V'={}&-\frac1c\int d\br\,\bj_{\rm e}(\br)\cdot\bA(\br)+\frac{e^2}{2m_ec^2}\int d\br\,\Psi^\dagger(\br)\Psi(\br)\,\bA^2(\br)\\&-\frac1c\sum_{ia\alpha\mu}\frac{1}{m_a}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}\pi_{ia\mu}A_\alpha(\bR^0_i)+\frac{1}{2c^2}\sum_{ia\mu\alpha\beta}\frac{1}{m_a}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}A_\alpha(\bR^0_i)A_\beta(\bR^0_i)\\&+\frac12\int d\br\int d\br'\,\frac{\big[\rho_{\rm e}(\br)+\rho_{\rm ion}(\br)\big]\big[\rho_{\rm e}(\br')+\rho_{\rm ion}(\br')\big]}{|\br-\br'|}.\end{aligned} \tag{E.237}$$

Here $\Psi(\br)=\sum_{n\bk}c_{n\bk}\phi_{n\bk}(\br)$ (E.240), $\bj_{\rm e}$ is the paramagnetic current (E.238), $\rho_{\rm ion}=-\nabla\cdot\bP$ with $P_\mu(\br)=\sum_{ia\nu}Z^*_{a\mu\nu}Q_{ia\nu}\delta(\br-\bR^0_i)$ (E.241), and the $\bA$ in $V'$ is the full field (E.216), all three polarizations included. Note what is absent: no term is written as an electron–phonon vertex $g\,c^\dagger c\,(a+a^\dagger)$, and there is no Debye–Waller term (the ionic $A^2$ term is a two-photon, not a two-phonon, vertex). Electrons and phonons interact only through the field: electrostatically through the $\rho_{\rm e}\rho_{\rm ion}$ cross term, which becomes the bare long-range Fröhlich vertex once $\bQ$ is quantized, and electrodynamically by exchanging a photon between $-\frac1c\bj_{\rm e}\cdot\bA$ and $-\frac1c Z^*\pi\cdot\bA/m_a$. The transverse photons bring retardation in EPP's sense (finite $c$), not Giustino's (frequency-dependent electronic screening). The first two terms of (E.236) are the first line of Giustino's (G.1) (§A.2).

Note on the source: two different $\bj_{\rm e}$

(E.166) defines the kinetic current $e\sum_e\mathbf v_e\delta(\br-\br_e)$, built from velocities and gauge invariant. The $\bj_{\rm e}$ in (E.237) must instead be the paramagnetic current

$$\bj_{\rm e}(\br)=\frac{e\hbar}{2\ii m_e}\Big\{\Psi^\dagger(\br)\nabla\Psi(\br)-\big[\nabla\Psi^\dagger(\br)\big]\Psi(\br)\Big\}, \tag{E.238}$$

which is what $-\frac{e}{2m_ec}\sum_e(\bp_e\cdot\bA+\bA\cdot\bp_e)$ in (E.186) becomes in second quantization. The two differ by the diamagnetic current: kinetic $=$ paramagnetic $-\frac{e^2}{m_ec}\Psi^\dagger\Psi\,\bA$. Using the kinetic current in (E.237) would triple the $A^2$ term.

What $H_0$ already contains

EPP flags double counting on p. 40 but does not resolve it here. The Kohn–Sham $E_{n\bk}$ already contain the Hartree and xc mean field, to which (E.235) adds the bare electron–electron interaction. The force constants in $H_0$ must be short-range, since the dipole–dipole part is regenerated here by $\rho_{\rm ion}V\rho_{\rm ion}$; the rule is set out in §B.1, where the basis phase that (E.167) and (E.241) also drop is discussed.

B.5EPP §§4.5–4.7, §5 · Eqs. 246–311

Propagators and the RPA photon self-energy

Free phonons and photons get their propagators, and matter enters the photon line through one current–current self-energy. By the end you can write the ionic part exactly, explain why gauge invariance fixes the diamagnetic term, and recognise the result as the Gonze–Lee infrared dielectric tensor.

§B.4 ended with the free Hamiltonian $H_0$ (E.236) of Kohn–Sham electrons, bare phonons and transverse photons, and an interaction $V'$ (E.237). Units are Gaussian, $Z^*$ carries the dimension of charge, and $f(\omega)=\int dt\,e^{i\omega t}f(t)$ (E.255). Names follow the page convention: EPP's photon propagator $D$, photon self-energy $\Pi$ (written $\Pi_{jj}$ from EPP §6 on) and phonon propagator $F$; Giustino's phonon Green's function is $\mathcal D$.

Temperature: the "$n_B=0$" rule

Everything below uses $T=0$ time-ordered propagators. EPP §4.5 argues that this costs nothing for bosons. After the continuation $i\omega_n\to\omega+i\eta$ (E.246), the Matsubara phonon propagator becomes the retarded one,

$$F^r_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=\frac1\hbar\,\frac{2\omega_\sigma(\bq)}{(\omega+i\eta)^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)},\tag{E.247}$$

which contains no temperature: for a harmonic field the commutator $[Q(t),Q(0)]$ is a c-number. The real-time time-ordered function at finite $T$ does depend on $T$,

$$F^T_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=2\,\frac{\omega_\sigma(\bq)}{\hbar}\left[\frac{1+n_{\bq\sigma}}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}-\frac{n_{\bq\sigma}}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)-i\eta}\right],\tag{E.249}$$

but only through its imaginary part, $-i\pi(1+2n_{\bq\sigma})\,\delta(\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2)$ times $2\omega_\sigma/\hbar$. EPP's rule follows: in time-ordered perturbation theory set $n_{\bq\sigma}=0$ in every boson line, keep the Fermi functions $f(T)$ in the electron bubbles, and make the $i\eta$ retarded at the end.

Where the rule holds, and where it does not

It holds for what EPP §§5–7 compute. Free boson lines and the ionic photon self-energy below (one harmonic phonon line) have $T$-independent retarded forms. Self-energies built from electron bubbles carry their temperature dependence in $f(T)$, as in Giustino's G Eq. 145. It fails when a boson line runs inside a fermion self-energy: Giustino's Fan–Migdal self-energy (G Eq. 158) carries $n_{\bq\nu}$ in its numerators, and that produces the temperature shift of band gaps (§A.7, §A.8). The figures below use retarded denominators $\omega^2-\omega_0^2+i\gamma\omega$; the time-ordered $+i\eta$ form has the wrong sign of ${\rm Im}$ at $\omega\lt 0$.

The free phonon line

With Mahan's definition and the dimensionless displacement $Q_{\bq\sigma}=a_{\bq\sigma}+a^\dagger_{-\bq\sigma}$,

$$F_\sigma(\bq;t-t')=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\left\langle\Phi^{\rm phon}_0\right|T\{Q_{\bq\sigma}(t)\,Q_{-\bq\sigma}(t')\}\left|\Phi^{\rm phon}_0\right\rangle,\tag{E.251}$$

the two time orderings give $e^{\mp i\omega_\sigma(t-t')}$ (E.254), and the Fourier transform adds them into

$$\boxed{F_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=\frac1\hbar\,\frac{2\omega_\sigma(\bq)}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}}\tag{E.256}$$

that is, $\frac1\hbar\big[\frac{1}{\omega-\omega_\sigma+i\eta}-\frac{1}{\omega+\omega_\sigma-i\eta}\big]$: the ordering $t>t'$ gives the pole at $+\omega_\sigma$, the ordering $t\lt t'$ the pole at $-\omega_\sigma$. Because $Q$ is dimensionless, $F$ has units of inverse energy.

Bridge to Giustino: the same phonon line

Giustino's adiabatic mode propagator is $\mathcal D^{\rm A}_{\bq\nu}(\omega)=\frac{1}{\omega-\omega_{\bq\nu}+i\eta}-\frac{1}{\omega+\omega_{\bq\nu}-i\eta}=\frac{2\omega_{\bq\nu}}{\omega^2-\omega^2_{\bq\nu}+i\eta}$ (G Eqs. 132, 134; §A.6), so $\mathcal D^{\rm A}_{\bq\nu}=\hbar F_\sigma$. One difference matters. EPP's $\omega_\sigma(\bq)$ are bare frequencies from short-range force constants, without LO–TO splitting; the photon line regenerates it in §B.7.

The free transverse photon line

The photon propagator is defined with the opposite sign and an extra $1/c$,

$$D^0_{\mu\nu}(\br,\br';t-t')=\frac{i}{\hbar c}\left\langle\Phi^{\rm phot}_0\right|T\{A_\mu(\br,t)\,A_\nu(\br',t')\}\left|\Phi^{\rm phot}_0\right\rangle,\tag{E.257}$$

a choice that makes $D$ the response of the vector potential to an external current, $\bA=D\,\bj^{\rm ext}$ (EPP p. 83). Split $\bA=\bA_t+\bA_l$ (E.258); the cross terms vanish (E.259). The transverse operators oscillate at $\omega_\bq=cq$, the time integral gives the same pole pair as for phonons, and the polarization sum is the transverse projector, $\sum_{\alpha=1,2}e_{\mu\alpha}(\bq)e_{\nu\alpha}(\bq)=\delta_{\mu\nu}-q_\mu q_\nu/q^2$:

$$\boxed{D^{0t}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-4\pi c\left[\delta_{\mu\nu}-\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{q^2}\right]\frac{1}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\bq+i\eta},\qquad\omega_\bq=qc.}\tag{E.261}$$

It is the Green's function of $(\omega^2/c^2-q^2)\bA_t=-\frac{4\pi}{c}\bj_t$. Its static limit, $\frac{4\pi}{cq^2}(\delta_{\mu\nu}-\hat q_\mu\hat q_\nu)$, is Biot–Savart. Between currents $j\sim\rho v$ it is weaker than Coulomb's $4\pi/q^2$ between charges by $(v/c)^2$, unless $cq\lesssim\omega$: the light cone of §X.1. (The printed intermediate step (E.260) duplicates a factor $2\omega_{\bq\alpha}$; (E.261) is correct. Clerical slips of this kind are collected in §Z.2.)

The longitudinal photon line vanishes; Coulomb does not

The longitudinal operators do not appear in $H_0$: the longitudinal field energy was moved into $V'$ as the Coulomb term (E.235). In the interaction picture they are frozen, $\omega_{\bq3}=0^+$ (E.262), the same steps give a propagator proportional to $\omega_{\bq3}$, and

$$\boxed{D^{0l}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=0.}\tag{E.263}$$

The retarded version vanishes too (E.267–E.268), because a static $\bA_l$ commutes with itself. Strictly, (E.263) holds for $\omega\neq0$: a time-independent $\bA_l$ inserted directly into (E.259) gives a term $\propto\delta(\omega)$.

This does not remove the longitudinal field. In the Heisenberg picture $\bA_l$ evolves, with $\bE^l=-\frac1c\dot\bA^l$ tied to the charges by Gauss's law (E.269), and that physics sits in the Coulomb term of $V'$. §B.6 rewrites that Coulomb term, through continuity, as the temporal-gauge propagator $D^{0l}$ of (E.374) between currents, and explains why (E.263) and (E.374) do not contradict each other.

Dressing the transverse photon

EPP §5 first drops the Coulomb term of $V'$ (E.270), so that only $\bA_t$ propagates. The ionic terms then take the form of the electronic ones once an ionic density tensor and an ionic current are defined,

$$\rho^{\rm ion}_{\alpha\beta}(\br)=\frac{m_0}{e^2}\sum_{ia\mu}\frac{1}{m_a}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}\,\delta(\br-\bR^0_i),\tag{E.271}$$
$$j^{\rm ion}_\alpha(\br)=\sum_{ia\mu}\frac{1}{m_a}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}\,\pi_{a\mu}(\br)\,\delta(\br-\bR^0_i).\tag{E.272}$$

$m_0$ is an arbitrary reference mass that cancels. (E.272) is the polarization current $Z^*\dot Q$ of point dipoles at the lattice sites, with $\dot Q\to\pi/m_a$; the rest of $\dot\bP$, $-\frac1c Z^*Z^*\bA/m_a$, is the ionic diamagnetic current, as $\bp\to\bp-\frac ec\bA$ for electrons. The interaction becomes four look-alike terms (E.273). Expanding the exact propagator (E.275) in the interaction picture (E.276) and summing the RPA diagrams gives

$$\boxed{\begin{aligned}D^t_{\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)={}&D^{0t}_{\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)\\&+\sum_{\alpha\beta}\int d^3\br_1\!\int d^3\br_2\,D^{0t}_{\mu\alpha}(\br,\br_1,\omega)\,\Pi^{\rm RPA}_{\alpha\beta}(\br_1,\br_2,\omega)\,D^t_{\beta\nu}(\br_2,\br',\omega)\end{aligned}}\tag{E.277}$$
=+

"RPA" means that the self-energy is the lowest-order irreducible insertion of each species: one bubble plus one contact term,

$$\Pi^{\rm RPA}_{\alpha\beta}(\br,\br',\omega)=\Pi^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\br,\br',\omega)+\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\alpha\beta}(\br,\br',\omega),\tag{E.278}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\Pi^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\br,\br',\omega)={}&\underbrace{-\frac{e^2}{mc}\,\rho^{\rm e}(\br)\,\delta(\br-\br')\,\delta_{\alpha\beta}}_{\Pi^{\rm e,dia}}\\&+\underbrace{\frac{i}{\hbar c}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dt\,e^{i\omega(t-t')}\left\langle\Phi^{\rm el}_0\right|T\{j^{\rm e}_\alpha(\br,t)\,j^{\rm e}_\beta(\br',t')\}\left|\Phi^{\rm el}_0\right\rangle}_{\Pi^{\rm e,para}},\end{aligned}\tag{E.279}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\alpha\beta}(\br,\br',\omega)={}&\underbrace{-\frac{e^2}{m_0c}\,\rho^{\rm ion}_{\alpha\beta}(\br)\,\delta(\br-\br')}_{\Pi^{\rm ion,dia}}\\&+\underbrace{\frac{i}{\hbar c}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dt\,e^{i\omega(t-t')}\left\langle\Phi^{\rm phon}_0\right|T\{j^{\rm ion}_\alpha(\br,t)\,j^{\rm ion}_\beta(\br',t')\}\left|\Phi^{\rm phon}_0\right\rangle}_{\Pi^{\rm ion,para}}.\end{aligned}\tag{E.280}$$

In (E.279) $\rho^{\rm e}$ means $\langle\rho^{\rm e}\rangle$; EPP says so only for the ions, whose contact term it derives from the two equivalent contractions of the $A\rho^{\rm ion}A$ vertex (factor 2, p. 59).

+ + +

Diagrams after EPP Fig. 7 (blue squares: electronic current vertices $-\frac1c\bj^{\rm e}\cdot\bA$; teal squares: ionic current vertices; dot: the electronic $A^2$ contact vertex; amber ring: the ionic $A^2$ contact at an ion site, drawn as in §B.4). Rose wavy stubs are transverse photons, the amber zigzag is the free phonon line (E.256). The ionic pair is exact for harmonic phonons. The resummation into (E.277) is deferred to EPP's "Lecture 9" notes, which are not part of the manuscript, and the printed series (E.276) should start at $n=0$ (§Z.2).

Physical picture: why two terms per species

Every charged species couples to $\bA$ twice: the paramagnetic vertex $-\frac1c\bj\cdot\bA$ absorbs or emits one photon, the $A^2$ vertex scatters two at one point. The contact term alone is the inertial response of free charges, as in a plasma. The bubble adds the restoring forces (springs for ions, gaps for electrons). In a slowly varying field bound charges only polarize, so in an insulator the two terms cancel exactly at $\omega=0$.

Bridge to Giustino: $W=v+vPW$ for photons

(E.277)–(E.278) have the algebra of Giustino's $W=v+vPW$ (G Eq. 90, §A.5): $D^{0t}\leftrightarrow v$, $\Pi\leftrightarrow P$, $D^t\leftrightarrow W$. Resumming the electrons first gives $D^t=D^t_{\rm e}+D^t_{\rm e}\Pi^{\rm ion}D^t$ with $D^t_{\rm e}=D^{0t}+D^{0t}\Pi^{\rm e}D^t_{\rm e}$, the transverse counterpart of his $W_{\rm e}$ (G Eq. 94) and of $W=W_{\rm e}+W_{\rm e}\mathcal DW_{\rm e}$ (G Eqs. 104–105). The vertices are now currents instead of densities, and the ions enter through the pre-screened Born charge $Z^*$ instead of the nuclear charge $Z_\kappa$. The ionic part is exact for harmonic phonons, because $j^{\rm ion}$ is linear in phonon operators. The electronic bubble has no vertex corrections (no excitons); a BSE current–current response in its place would give exciton polaritons.

Gauge invariance fixes the diamagnetic term

In the temporal gauge $\bE=\frac{i\omega}{c}\bA$, so a static, uniform $\bA$ carries no field at all. It is a pure gauge, and in a normal (non-superconducting) system it must drive no current: $\Pi(\bq\to0,\omega=0)=0$. The diamagnetic term is frequency independent, so it must equal minus the static paramagnetic term. EPP uses this (proved in its Lecture 9 notes for quasi-2D crystals) to write the electronic self-energy of a crystal without any explicit diamagnetic term,

$$\boxed{\Pi^{\rm RPA,e}_{\alpha\beta\bG\bG'}(\bq,\omega)=\Pi^{\rm para,e}_{\alpha\beta\bG\bG'}(\bq,\omega)-\Pi^{\rm para,e}_{\alpha\beta\bG\bG'}(\bq,\omega=0)}\tag{E.281}$$

In optics language, $\bj=\Pi\bA$ and $\bE=\frac{i\omega}{c}\bA$ give $\sigma=-\frac{ic}{\omega}\Pi$ and $\epsilon(\omega)=1+\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\Pi(\omega)$ (not written in EPP), so $-4\pi c\,\Pi$ has units of frequency squared. At $\bq=0$ a free electron gas has only the contact term, $\Pi=-ne^2/mc$, which gives the Drude $\epsilon=1-\omega_p^2/\omega^2$ with $\omega_p^2=4\pi ne^2/m$. The paramagnetic part in a crystal is

$$\Pi^{\rm para,e}_{\alpha\beta\bG\bG'}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{2}{c\Omega}\sum_{\bk\in{\rm BZ}}\sum_{nm}\frac{f_{n\bk}-f_{m\bk+\bq}}{\hbar\omega+E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}+i\eta}\;j^\alpha_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\bG)\left[j^\beta_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\bG')\right]^*,\tag{E.282}$$
$$j^\alpha_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\br)=\frac{e\hbar}{2im}\left\{\phi^*_{n\bk}(\br)\,\partial_\alpha\phi_{m\bk+\bq}(\br)-\left[\partial_\alpha\phi^*_{n\bk}(\br)\right]\phi_{m\bk+\bq}(\br)\right\},\tag{E.284}$$

with $j^\alpha(\bG)=\int d\br\,e^{-i(\bq+\bG)\cdot\br}j^\alpha(\br)$ over the crystal (E.283). The factor 2 is spin, $\Omega$ is the crystal volume, and $\phi_{n\bk}$ is normalized over the crystal. For a strictly 2D sheet in a supercell of period $l$, EPP takes $\Pi^{\rm RPA,e,2D}_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega)=l\,\Pi^{\rm RPA,e}_{\alpha\beta,\bG=\bG'=0}(\bQ,\omega)$ (after E.285; used in §B.10).

Bridge to your RPA code: Adler–Wiser with currents

(E.282) is the Adler–Wiser $\chi^0_{\bG\bG'}(\bq,\omega)$ of RPA and GW codes, with the density vertices $\langle n\bk|e^{-i(\bq+\bG)\cdot\br}|m\bk+\bq\rangle$ replaced by current vertices and an overall factor $-1/c$. In the optical limit $j^\alpha_{n\bk,m\bk}(\bG=0)=\frac{e}{m}\langle n\bk|\hat p_\alpha|m\bk\rangle$, the momentum matrix elements of velocity-gauge optics. Giustino's $P_{\rm e}$ (G Eq. 92) is the density version; §B.6 shows that continuity turns one into the other.

What (E.281) buys in practice

Exactly, "dia + para" and (E.281) agree. In practice band sums are truncated, and with nonlocal pseudopotentials the velocity operator is $\frac{i}{\hbar}[H,\br]$ rather than $\bp/m$, so the computed $\Pi^{\rm para}(0)$ no longer cancels $ne^2/mc$ exactly. A naive "dia + para" then leaves $-(1-S)\,\omega_p^2/\omega^2$ in $\epsilon$, with $S$ the fraction of the f-sum that the bubble captures: for $S\lt 1$, a Drude term in an insulator. (E.281) enforces $\Pi(0)=0$ by construction. It also sets to zero the true static transverse response at finite $q$, the orbital magnetic susceptibility of order $q^2$, which is negligible for optics.

The ionic self-energy, exactly

Inserting (E.272) into (E.280) leaves a momentum–momentum correlator of point ions (E.286). The momentum (E.274) is linear in $a,a^\dagger$, so only the $aa^\dagger$ and $a^\dagger a$ contractions survive, the occupation factors cancel in the principal part, and after the lattice sums the result is the same for every $\bG,\bG'$. It is compact in terms of the ionic current vertex

$$\boxed{j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)=\sum_{a\mu}\frac{Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}}{\sqrt{m_a}}\,e_{a\mu\sigma}(\bq)}\tag{E.295}$$

the Born-charge dipole that mode $\sigma$ carries per unit mass-weighted amplitude, in units of charge per $\sqrt{\rm mass}$. It vanishes for nonpolar modes, and for acoustic modes at $\bq\to0$ because the Born charges obey $\sum_aZ^*_a=0$. With the conjugate vertex $j^*_{\beta\sigma}$ (E.296),

$$\boxed{\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta,\bG\bG'}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{1}{c\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\frac{\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}\,j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\,j^*_{\beta\sigma}(\bq)}\tag{E.297}$$
$$\boxed{\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{\hbar}{c\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\frac{\omega_\sigma(\bq)}{2}\,F_\sigma(\bq,\omega)\,j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\,j^*_{\beta\sigma}(\bq)}\tag{E.299}$$

(E.299) is "vertex, phonon line, vertex", the third diagram above. Here $\sigma$ labels the $3s$ branches and $\alpha,\beta,\mu,\nu$ are Cartesian ((E.287) still uses $\alpha,\beta$ for branches). The 2D sheet version has $S_{\rm uc}$ and $\delta(z)\delta(z')$ (E.300).

Derivation: from (E.286) to (E.297)

With $a_{\bq\sigma}(t)=a_{\bq\sigma}e^{-i\omega_\sigma t}$, the surviving contractions force $\bq'=-\bq$ and equal branches. The time integrals $\int d\tau\,e^{i\omega\tau}\theta(\pm\tau)e^{\mp i\omega_\sigma\tau}$ produce the pole pair, and with $e_{a\mu\sigma}(-\bq)=e^*_{a\mu\sigma}(\bq)$ (E.288) the pairs recombine into (EPP p. 62)

$$\begin{aligned}\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\br,\br',\omega)={}&-\frac{1}{\hbar c}\frac1N\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\sum_{\bq\in{\rm BZ}}\sum_{ia\mu}\sum_{jb\nu}\frac{Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{b\beta\nu}}{\sqrt{m_am_b}}\,\hbar\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)\,e_{a\mu\sigma}(\bq)e^*_{b\nu\sigma}(\bq)\,e^{i\bq(\br-\br')}\\&\times\left\{\frac{1+n_{\bq\sigma}}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}-\frac{n_{\bq\sigma}}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)-i\eta}\right\}\delta(\br-\bR^0_i)\,\delta(\br'-\bR^0_j).\end{aligned}\tag{E.289}$$

The bracket is that of (E.249); $n_{\bq\sigma}=0$ gives (E.290). The lattice sums use $\sum_i\delta(\br-\bR^0_i)=\Omega_{\rm uc}^{-1}\sum_\bG e^{i\bG\cdot\br}$. Together with $\sum_\bq\to\frac{\Omega}{(2\pi)^3}\int d\bq$ (E.291) they give the prefactor $\frac{\Omega}{N}\frac{N^2}{\Omega^2}=\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}$ and a bracket that does not depend on $\bG,\bG'$ (E.293). Comparing with the crystal form $f(\br,\br')=\sum_{\bG\bG'}\int_{\rm BZ}\frac{d\bq}{(2\pi)^3}f_{\bG\bG'}(\bq)e^{i(\bq+\bG)\cdot\br}e^{-i(\bq+\bG')\cdot\br'}$ (E.294) reads off (E.297). The diamagnetic term (E.302) goes through the same lattice sum, plus an implicit relabelling $\bG+\bG'\to\bG$, to (E.304).

The $\bG$-independence is an artefact of putting every atom of the cell at $\bR^0_i$. The response is that of a grating of point dipoles, and EPP warns that its Bragg components are unphysical; only $\bG=\bG'=0$ should be used.

The diamagnetic part follows from (E.271) and (E.280). It is local, $\propto\delta(\br-\bR^0_i)\delta(\br-\br')$ (E.302), and after the same lattice sum it is constant in $\bq$, $\omega$, $\bG$ and $\bG'$:

$$\boxed{\Pi^{\rm ion,dia}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}c}\sum_{a\mu}\frac{1}{m_a}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}}\tag{E.304}$$

For isotropic Born charges $-4\pi c\,\Pi^{\rm ion,dia}=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_aZ^{*2}_a/m_a\equiv\Omega_p^2$, the ionic plasma frequency of ions with the springs cut; for a diatomic crystal it is the $\omega_p^2$ defined with (E.152) in §B.3.

Completeness: the diamagnetic term is minus the static bubble

Set $\omega=0$ in (E.297). There are no real excitations at zero frequency, so $\eta\to0$ and every mode contributes its full strength (E.306):

$$\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega=0)=\frac{1}{c\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\,j^*_{\beta\sigma}(\bq).\tag{E.307}$$

Insert the vertices (E.308) and use the completeness of the dynamical-matrix eigenvectors, $\sum_\sigma e_{a\mu\sigma}(\bq)e^*_{b\nu\sigma}(\bq)=\delta_{ab}\delta_{\mu\nu}$ (E.28):

$$\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega=0)=\frac{1}{c\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{a\mu}\frac{Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}}{m_a},\tag{E.309}$$
$$\boxed{\Pi^{\rm ion,dia}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)=-\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega=0)}\tag{E.310}$$

Neither the force constants nor $\bq$ survive. Read as a statement about modes, (E.309) is an oscillator-strength sum rule, $\sum_\sigma j_{\alpha\sigma}j^*_{\beta\sigma}=\sum_{a\mu}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}/m_a$: springs move infrared strength between modes but cannot change its total. It is the ionic Thomas–Reiche–Kuhn rule.

Note on the source: the argument in §5.2.2

EPP first motivates (E.310) with $\nabla\cdot\bj^{\rm ion}=0$ (E.301), because "there are no free charges". But the ions carry the bound charge $-\nabla\cdot\bP$, used in §6 (E.313), and (E.301) with (E.350) would force $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}=0$. The right reason is gauge invariance; the result stands because §5.2.3 proves it through completeness. At exactly $\bq=0$ the acoustic terms of (E.306) are $0/0$: take $\omega\to0$ first.

The infrared dielectric tensor

Combining (E.297), (E.304) and (E.310),

$$\boxed{\Pi^{\rm ion,RPA}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)=\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)-\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega=0)}\tag{E.311}$$

has the same structure as (E.281). With $\frac{\omega_\sigma^2}{\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2}+1=\frac{\omega^2}{\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2}$ it reads, in the form EPP writes out in §6,

$$\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{\omega^2}{c\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\frac{j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)\,j^*_{\nu\sigma}(\bq)}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}.\tag{E.352}$$

It vanishes at $\omega=0$, and for $\omega\gg\omega_\sigma$ it tends to the contact term: far above the phonons the lattice responds as free ions. Now add the electrons far below the gap, where $4\pi c\,\Pi^{\rm e}\approx(\epsilon^\infty-1)\omega^2$, and use $\epsilon=1+4\pi c\,\Pi/\omega^2$. At $\bq\to0$ this gives (derived, not printed in EPP)

$$\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}(\omega)=\epsilon^\infty_{\alpha\beta}+\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma}\frac{j_{\alpha\sigma}\,j^*_{\beta\sigma}}{\omega_\sigma^2-\omega^2-i\eta},$$

the infrared dielectric tensor of Gonze and Lee (1997), the DFPT reference Giustino cites for the LO–TO splitting (§VI.A.3), with $j_{\alpha\sigma}j^*_{\beta\sigma}$ their mode oscillator strength $S_{\sigma,\alpha\beta}$ (up to the $e^2$ inside EPP's $Z^*$). The ingredients are standard DFPT output, but in EPP the formula is derived: the poles are the bare short-range frequencies and $\epsilon^\infty$ comes from $\Pi^{\rm e}$. For one polar mode its zero is $\omega_{\rm LO}^2=\omega_{\rm TO}^2+\Omega_p^2/\epsilon^\infty$ (§B.3, §B.7).

Bridge to Giustino: the photon self-energy is the dual of the phonon self-energy

Giustino's phonon self-energy has the same structure, $\Pi^{\rm ph}\propto Z_\kappa Z_{\kappa'}\partial\partial'[W_{\rm e}(\omega)-W_{\rm e}(0)]$ (G Eq. 121, §A.5), enforced by the acoustic sum rule (G Eq. 120): translation invariance kills the static response to a rigid shift of the lattice, as gauge invariance here kills the static response to a uniform $\bA$. The $\chi^0(\omega)-\chi^0(0)$ in Giustino's nonadiabatic $\Pi^{\rm NA}$ (G Eq. 145, §A.6) looks alike but serves another purpose, avoiding double counting of the adiabatic part. Through continuity (§B.6), (E.352) also fixes the ionic density response $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\bq\cdot\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}\cdot\bq$ that drives the LO phonon and the Fröhlich coupling.

B.6EPP §6 · Eqs. 312–385

Charge conservation, the total propagator and polaritons

Coulomb lines and photon lines, charge vertices and current vertices: EPP §6 shows that charge conservation collapses all of them into one $3\times3$ Dyson equation, $D=D^0+D^0\Pi_{jj}D$. By the end you can derive it, read $D^0$ as the vacuum Maxwell propagator, and find plasmons, LO phonons and polaritons as its poles.

§B.5 dressed the transverse photon (E Eq. 277) and kept the Coulomb interaction (E Eq. 235) as a separate, instantaneous scalar line $v$. EPP §6 puts both into one perturbation series. Units are Gaussian, $v(q)=4\pi/q^2$, with the charges in the vertices; the Born charges $Z^*$ carry the dimension of charge. Giustino's nuclear density correlator $D$ (G Eq. 103) is written $\mathcal D$, so that $D$ always means EPP's photon propagator.

Physical picture: one current, two ways to look at it

A crystal has one response to the field: an induced current. Charge piles up only where that current converges, $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot\bj=0$. So the density response of GW, BSE and DFPT is the longitudinal part of the current response, and the instantaneous Coulomb line is the longitudinal part of the photon line. With both statements, every line is a $3\times3$ tensor, every bubble a current–current correlator, and the series sums into one Dyson equation. In an isotropic medium it splits into a longitudinal channel, whose poles are plasmons and LO phonons, and a transverse channel, whose poles are polaritons.

One interaction, two kinds of lines

Adding the longitudinal term of E Eq. 235 to the transverse couplings of §B.5 gives the full interaction (EPP p. 68):

$$\begin{aligned}V'={}&-\frac1c\int d\br\,\bj^{\rm e}(\br)\cdot\bA(\br)+\frac{e^2}{2m_{\rm e}c^2}\int d\br\,\rho^{\rm e}(\br)\,\bA^2(\br)\\&-\frac1c\int d\br\,\bj^{\rm ion}(\br)\cdot\bA(\br)+\frac{e^2}{2m_0c^2}\sum_{\alpha\beta}\int d\br\,A_\alpha(\br)\,\rho^{\rm ion}_{\alpha\beta}(\br)\,A_\beta(\br)\\&+\frac12\int d\br\int d\br'\,\frac{[\rho^{\rm e}(\br)+\rho^{\rm ion}(\br)][\rho^{\rm e}(\br')+\rho^{\rm ion}(\br')]}{|\br-\br'|}\end{aligned}\tag{E.312}$$

The ionic bound charge $\rho^{\rm ion}=-\nabla\cdot\bP$ of the point dipoles $P_\mu(\br)=\sum_{ia\nu}Z^*_{a\mu\nu}Q_{ia\nu}\,\delta(\br-\bR^0_i)$ (E Eqs. 313–314) is linear in the phonon operators. The c-number tensor $\rho^{\rm ion}_{\alpha\beta}\propto\sum_aZ^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}/m_a$ (E Eq. 315) belongs to the diamagnetic term. Mixed electron–ion bubbles vanish at lowest order, so $D=D^0+D^{1,\rm ion}+D^{1,\rm e}+\dots$ (E Eq. 316), each term a $4\times4$ matrix with one scalar (Coulomb) slot and a $3\times3$ vector block:

$$D^0=\begin{bmatrix}v&0\\0&\hat D^{0t}\end{bmatrix}\tag{E.317}$$
$$D^{1,i}=\begin{bmatrix}v\,\Pi^i_{\rho\rho}\,v&v\,\Pi^i_{\rho j}\,\hat D^{0t}\\ \hat D^{0t}\,\Pi^i_{j\rho}\,v&\hat D^{0t}\,\Pi^i_{jj}\,\hat D^{0t}\end{bmatrix},\qquad i={\rm e,\,ion}\tag{E.319}$$

$\hat D^{0t}_{\mu\nu}=\frac{i}{\hbar c}\langle T\{A_\mu A_\nu\}\rangle$ (E Eq. 318) is the transverse photon. The longitudinal pairing of the quantized field vanishes (E Eq. 263), so $v$ alone carries the longitudinal interaction. $\Pi^i_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle T\{\rho^i\rho^i\}\rangle$ (E Eq. 320) is Hedin's irreducible polarizability $P$, here the bare RPA bubble, and $\Pi^i_{jj}$ the gauge-invariant (para plus dia) current correlator (E Eqs. 321–322). Each sector has its own series, and at higher order the lines mix: a transverse photon can sit inside the Coulomb sector (EPP Fig. 8).

Induced charges and currents

Cut a diagram open and attach an external source. It is either a charge $\rho^{\rm ext}$, acting through $v$ (or $W$ once screened), or a vector potential coupled through $-\frac1c\int\bj\cdot\bA^{\rm ext}$, which does not distinguish $l$ from $t$. The bubbles are irreducible, so (EPP p. 72; $\otimes$ is a convolution in space and time)

$$\rho^{i,{\rm ind},l}=\Pi^i_{\rho\rho}\otimes W\otimes\rho^{\rm ext},\qquad i={\rm e,\,ion}\tag{E.330}$$
$$j^{i,{\rm ind}}_\mu=\sum_\nu\Pi^i_{jj\mu\nu}\otimes A^{{\rm ext,sc}}_\nu\tag{E.333}$$

and likewise $\rho^{i,\rm ind}=\sum_\mu\Pi^i_{\rho j\mu}\otimes A^{\rm ext,sc}_\mu$ and $j^{i,{\rm ind},l}_\mu=\Pi^i_{j\rho\mu}\otimes W\otimes\rho^{\rm ext}$ (E Eqs. 331–332), with $\bA^{\rm ext,sc}$ the screened external field. This is the identity $\chi v=PW$ for both kinds of probe. With time dependence $e^{-i\omega t}$, the temporal gauge and continuity read

$$\bE^{{\rm ext},\sigma,{\rm sc}}(\omega)=i\frac{\omega}{c}\,\bA^{{\rm ext},\sigma,{\rm sc}}(\omega),\qquad\sigma=l,t\tag{E.334}$$
$$\nabla\cdot\bj=i\omega\rho\tag{E.335}$$

Charge conservation: the connection formulas

Impose continuity on the pair induced by the longitudinal probe (E Eq. 340) and on the pair induced by the total field (E Eq. 342). Since $\rho^{\rm ext}$ and $\bA^{\rm ext,sc}$ are arbitrary and $W$ is invertible, the kernels themselves must agree (EPP p. 73):

$$\Pi^i_{\rho\rho}(\br,\br',\omega)=-\frac{i}{\omega}\sum_\mu\partial_\mu\Pi^i_{j\rho\mu}(\br,\br',\omega)\tag{E.341}$$
$$\Pi^i_{\rho j\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)=-\frac{i}{\omega}\sum_\mu\partial_\mu\Pi^i_{jj\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)\tag{E.344}$$

The mixed correlators carry different prefactors, $\Pi_{j\rho}=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle T\{j\rho\}\rangle$ and $\Pi_{\rho j}=+\frac{i}{\hbar c}\langle T\{\rho j\}\rangle$ (E Eqs. 345–346), because a current vertex always comes from $-\frac1c\int\bj\cdot\bA$. Reversing the operator order in a time-ordered correlator gives

$$\Pi^i_{\rho j\mu}(\br',\br,\omega)=-\frac1c\,\Pi^i_{j\rho\mu}(\br,\br',-\omega)\tag{E.347}$$

and $\Pi^i_{jj\mu\nu}(\br,\br',-\omega)=\Pi^i_{jj\nu\mu}(\br',\br,\omega)$ (E Eq. 348). These move the derivative of E Eq. 344 onto $\br'$, and E Eq. 341 closes the set:

$$\Pi^i_{j\rho\mu}(\br,\br',\omega)=-i\frac{c}{\omega}\sum_\nu\partial'_\nu\Pi^i_{jj\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)\tag{E.349}$$
$$\boxed{\Pi^i_{\rho\rho}(\br,\br',\omega)=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\sum_{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu\,\Pi^i_{jj\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)}\tag{E.350}$$

In a homogeneous medium, with $\partial_\mu\to iq_\mu$ and $\partial'_\nu\to-iq_\nu$ (derived from E Eqs. 344, 349 and 350):

$$\Pi_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,\bq\cdot\Pi_{jj}\cdot\bq,\qquad \Pi_{\rho j}=\frac1\omega\,\bq\cdot\Pi_{jj},\qquad \Pi_{j\rho}=-\frac{c}{\omega}\,\Pi_{jj}\cdot\bq .$$

These are the Ward identities of QED, $q_\mu\Pi^{\mu\nu}=0$ for the four-current, written for a crystal. Only $\Pi_{jj}$ is independent. The density response is its longitudinal projection, and a transverse current ($\bq\cdot\bj=0$) carries no charge.

EPP §6.0.2 verifies E Eq. 350 for the ions. $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}$ computed directly from $\rho^{\rm ion}=-\nabla\cdot\bP$ is, at $\bG=\bG'=0$ (cf. EPP p. 77),

$$\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}(\bq,\omega)=\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_\sigma\frac{|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma(\bq)|^2}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta},$$

which is exactly $-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\bq\cdot\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}\cdot\bq$ for the gauge-invariant correlator of §B.5,

$$\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{\omega^2}{c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\frac{j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)\,j^*_{\nu\sigma}(\bq)}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}.\tag{E.352}$$

Its overall $\omega^2$ comes from the diamagnetic subtraction $-\Pi^{\rm para}(0)$. The paramagnetic part alone would add $-\sum_\sigma|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2/(\Omega_{\rm uc}\omega^2)$, a static density response that diverges (third tab of the figure below). The numerator $\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma=\sum_a\bq\cdot Z^*_a\cdot\be_{a\sigma}/\sqrt{m_a}$ is that of the Verdi–Giustino vertex (G Eq. 180).

Derivation: from E Eqs. 341 and 344 to E Eqs. 349 and 350, and the ionic check

By E Eq. 347, $\Pi_{j\rho\mu}(\br,\br',\omega)=-c\,\Pi_{\rho j\mu}(\br',\br,-\omega)$. E Eq. 344 with $\br\leftrightarrow\br'$ and $\omega\to-\omega$ gives $\Pi_{\rho j\mu}(\br',\br,-\omega)=\frac{i}{\omega}\sum_\nu\partial'_\nu\Pi_{jj\nu\mu}(\br',\br,-\omega)$, and E Eq. 348 turns the last factor into $\Pi_{jj\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)$: this is E Eq. 349. Inserted into E Eq. 341 it gives the prefactor $(-\frac{i}{\omega})(-i\frac{c}{\omega})=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}$: E Eq. 350.

Ionic check: $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\sum_{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu\langle T\{P_\mu P_\nu\}\rangle$ (E Eq. 353). The displacement operator brings $\hbar/(2m_a\omega_\sigma)$ and the Fourier-transformed phonon pairing $2i\omega_\sigma/(\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2+i\eta)$, so the prefactor is $-\frac{i}{N\hbar}\cdot\frac{\hbar}{2\omega_\sigma}\cdot2i\omega_\sigma=\frac1N$, and the lattice sums (E Eq. 354) turn $\frac1N$ into $\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}$. The kernel $\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_\sigma j_{\mu\sigma}j^*_{\nu\sigma}/(\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2)$ is $-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj\mu\nu}$ by E Eq. 352. With the paramagnetic part alone, $\Pi^{\rm para}_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{1}{c\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_\sigma\omega_\sigma^2j_{\mu\sigma}j^*_{\nu\sigma}/(\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2)$ (E Eq. 297), the same contraction gives $\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_\sigma|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2\frac{\omega_\sigma^2}{\omega^2(\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2)}$, the direct result minus $\frac{1}{\Omega_{\rm uc}\omega^2}\sum_\sigma|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2$.

For the GW/BSE practitioner: length and velocity gauge

E Eq. 350 is why a length-gauge calculation with $\langle c|e^{-i\bq\cdot\br}|v\rangle$ and a velocity-gauge one with $\langle c|\hat\bp|v\rangle=im\omega_{cv}\langle c|\br|v\rangle$ give the same $\epsilon$. In E Eq. 383 below, the diamagnetic subtraction that makes it hold appears as the factor $\hbar\omega/(E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq})$. The $1/\omega^2$ divergence of velocity-gauge spectra computed without the diamagnetic term violates it. The current must also obey continuity with the Hamiltonian: nonlocal pseudopotentials require the correction $\frac{ie}{\hbar}[V_{\rm NL},\br]$ to the current of E Eq. 384. EPP verifies E Eq. 350 only for the ionic RPA correlator and concludes "inductively" that all connection formulas hold. They do, provided $\Pi_{jj}$ contains the diamagnetic term and the current operator obeys continuity with the Hamiltonian.

From four sectors to one tensor (EPP §6.0.3)

With E Eqs. 344, 349 and 350 every lowest-order sector contains only $\Pi_{jj}$ (EPP Fig. 9). EPP labels the scalar (Coulomb) slot of the $4\times4$ matrix "1", so $D_{11}$ is the scalar–scalar entry, not the $xx$ component. The Coulomb sector reads

$$\begin{aligned}D_{11}(\br,\br',\omega)={}&v(\br,\br')\\&-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\sum_{i={\rm e,ion}}\sum_{\alpha\beta=xyz}\int d\br_1d\br_2\,v(\br,\br_1)\big[\partial_{1\alpha}\partial_{2\beta}\Pi^i_{jj\alpha\beta}(\br_1,\br_2,\omega)\big]v(\br_2,\br')+\dots\end{aligned}\tag{E.355}$$

Integrating by parts moves the derivatives onto the Coulomb lines (EPP p. 79), but the sectors remain a scalar, a row, a column and a matrix. EPP acts on them with $-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu$ (E Eq. 359), $i\frac{c}{\omega}\partial_\mu$, $\frac{i}{\omega}\partial'_\nu$ and $1$. In our reading (EPP does not say so) this is a change to the temporal gauge: a potential $\phi(\br)$ becomes $\bA_l=\frac{ic}{\omega}\nabla\phi$, and a charge source becomes a current source through $\rho=-\frac{i}{\omega}\nabla'\cdot\bj$. Every Coulomb line then appears as

$$\boxed{D^{0l}_{\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu\,v(\br-\br')}\tag{E.364}$$

and all four sectors share the form $D^{ab}=\delta_{ab}D^{0a}+D^{0a}\Pi_{jj}D^{0b}+\dots$ with $a,b\in\{l,t\}$ (E Eqs. 365–368, EPP Fig. 10). The rule is

$$\rho^i\to j^i_\mu\quad(i={\rm ion,e}),\qquad v\to D^{0l}_{\mu\nu}(\omega),\tag{E.377}$$

and the sum is $D=D^0+D^0\Pi_{jj}D^0+\dots$ with $D^0=D^{0l}+D^{0t}$ and $\Pi_{jj}=\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}+\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj}$ (E Eqs. 369–371). The second tab of the figure below steps through EPP Figs. 9–11.

What $D^0$ is: the vacuum Maxwell propagator (EPP §6.0.4)

Fourier-transforming E Eq. 364 (E Eq. 373) and adding the transverse photon, with $\omega_\bq=cq$:

$$D^{0t}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{q^2}\,\frac{q^2\delta_{\mu\nu}-q_\mu q_\nu}{\omega^2-\omega_\bq^2+i\eta},\tag{E.372}$$
$$D^{0l}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{q^2}\,\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{\omega^2},\tag{E.374}$$
$$D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=D^{0l}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)+D^{0t}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\,\frac{-q_\mu q_\nu+\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}\delta_{\mu\nu}}{q^2-\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}-i\eta}.\tag{E.375}$$

In projector form, $D^0=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}P^L+\frac{4\pi}{c}\frac{P^T}{q^2-\omega^2/c^2}$ with $P^L=\hat q\hat q$ and $P^T=1-\hat q\hat q$. This is the inverse of the temporal-gauge Maxwell operator: $[(q^2-\frac{\omega^2}{c^2})\delta_{\mu\nu}-q_\mu q_\nu]A_\nu=\frac{4\pi}{c}j_\mu$ (derived here; EPP cites its "Lecture 9"). So $D^0\bj^{\rm ext}$ is the field of an external current, and $D^0\Pi_{jj}D^0\bj^{\rm ext}$ the first induced field (E Eq. 376). The longitudinal part $-4\pi c/\omega^2$ is independent of $q$: it has no light cone. Where $D^{0t}$ competes with it is the subject of §X.1.

Is the longitudinal propagator zero or not? E Eq. 263 vs E Eq. 374

Both statements are correct, and they are about different objects.

  • E Eq. 263, $D^{0l}=0$ (§B.5), is the free propagator of the interaction-picture operator $\bA_l$, which has no restoring force. Its field energy $\frac{1}{8\pi}\int\bE_l^2$ became, through Gauss's law, the Coulomb term of E Eq. 312 and was moved into $V'$ (§B.4). An operator with no dynamics in $H_0$ is static in the interaction picture, so its free propagator vanishes at every $\omega\neq0$ (only a $\delta(\omega)$ term remains). Hence $\hat D^{0t}$ is the only vector line in E Eq. 317.
  • E Eq. 374 is not a new line. It is the Coulomb line $v$ of E Eq. 312, carried by the connection formulas from charge vertices to current vertices. EPP calls E Eq. 364 "ad hoc", but $\bA_l=\frac{ic}{\omega}\nabla\phi$ and continuity fix it.

Keeping $v$ and adding $D^{0l}$ would count Coulomb twice. The $1/\omega^2$ double pole of E Eq. 374, for which EPP gives no $i\eta$, describes a static charge in the temporal gauge, where $\bA_l$ grows linearly in time at constant $\bE$. It is harmless because $D^{0l}$ only meets conserved currents, and $\bq\cdot\bj=\omega\rho$ supplies the compensating powers of $\omega$. Likewise, "identical to the vacuum Maxwell propagator" holds in the temporal gauge: photon propagators are gauge dependent, and only their action on conserved currents is not.

One Dyson equation

At higher order each sector mixes both lines and all vertex types (EPP §6.0.5, Fig. 11a). E Eq. 377 maps every diagram to current vertices joined by $D^{0l}$ and $D^{0t}$. Compatible diagrams sum into $D^0$ lines and the bubbles into $\Pi_{jj}$, so the series is geometric (E Eq. 378):

$$D=D^0+D^0\,\Pi_{jj}\,D,\qquad D^0=D^{0l}+D^{0t},\qquad \Pi_{jj}=\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj}+\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}.\tag{E.379}$$

In $(\bq,\omega)$ space, with $D^0$ from E Eq. 375 (repeated as E Eq. 381) and $\Pi_{jj}=\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}+\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj}$ (E Eq. 382):

$$D_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)+\sum_{\alpha\beta=xyz}D^0_{\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)\,\Pi_{jj\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,D_{\beta\nu}(\bq,\omega).\tag{E.380}$$

The ionic part is E Eq. 352 (repeated as E Eq. 385). The electronic part is the "para minus static para" form of §B.5, with the current vertices of E Eq. 384:

$$\begin{aligned}\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)&=\Pi^{\rm para,e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)-\Pi^{\rm para,e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega=0)\\&=\frac{2}{c\Omega}\sum_{\bk\in{\rm BZ}}\sum_{nm}\frac{\hbar\omega}{E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}}\,\frac{f_{n\bk}-f_{m\bk+\bq}}{\hbar\omega+E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}+i\eta}\,j^\mu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}\big[j^\nu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}\big]^*\end{aligned}\tag{E.383}$$

Here $\Omega=N\Omega_{\rm uc}$ is the crystal volume, $f$ are occupations and the 2 counts spin. $D$ propagates the total field $\bA^l+\bA^t$ in a crystal of electrons and phonons: "$W$ with photons". It is RPA: lowest-order irreducible bubbles, no mixed electron–ion bubbles, no exchange–correlation kernel and, from E Eq. 380 on, no crystal local fields ($\bG=\bG'=0$).

Isotropic medium: plasmons, LO phonons and polaritons

In an isotropic medium, or a cubic crystal at small $q$, both $\Pi_{jj}=\Pi_LP^L+\Pi_TP^T$ and $D^0$ are diagonal in the projectors. E Eq. 380 decouples and $D^{lt}=D^{tl}=0$ to all orders (derived here, not in the manuscript):

$$D_L(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2\,\epsilon_L(\bq,\omega)},\qquad D_T(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2\epsilon_T(\bq,\omega)-c^2q^2},\qquad \epsilon_{L,T}=1+\frac{4\pi c\,\Pi_{L,T}}{\omega^2}.$$

By E Eq. 350, $\epsilon_L=1-v\Pi_{\rho\rho}$, the RPA dielectric function of GW and BSE. The two channels have different poles.

  • $\epsilon_L(\bq,\omega)=0$: longitudinal modes, Coulomb dressed by matter. They do not depend on $c$, because $c\,\Pi_{jj}$ does not. A Drude metal gives the plasmon at $\omega_p$. A polar crystal, $\epsilon=\epsilon_\infty+\Omega_p^2/(\omega_{TO}^2-\omega^2)$ with $\Omega_p^2=4\pi|j|^2/\Omega_{\rm uc}$ for one mode of E Eq. 352, gives the LO phonon at $\omega_{LO}^2=\omega_{TO}^2+\Omega_p^2/\epsilon_\infty$. Here $\omega_{TO}$ is the bare $\omega_\sigma$, since the Dyson route has no local field.
  • $c^2q^2=\omega^2\epsilon_T(\bq,\omega)$: transverse modes, light dressed by matter. For the polar crystal these are the phonon polaritons
$$\omega_\pm^2=\frac{(\epsilon_\infty\omega_{LO}^2+c^2q^2)\pm\sqrt{(\epsilon_\infty\omega_{LO}^2+c^2q^2)^2-4\epsilon_\infty c^2q^2\omega_{TO}^2}}{2\epsilon_\infty}.$$

The upper branch starts at $\omega_{LO}$ at $q=0$, where $L$ and $T$ cannot be told apart. The lower branch tends to $\omega_{TO}$ for $cq\gg\sqrt{\epsilon_0}\,\omega_{TO}$. Between them $\epsilon\lt0$ and no transverse mode exists: the Reststrahlen band. §B.7 obtains the same branches from the phonon side and follows the order of the limits $q\to0$ and $c\to\infty$.

Derivation: L and T decouple, $D_{11}=W$, and the polariton roots

Write $D^0=d_LP^L+d_TP^T$ with $d_L=-4\pi c/\omega^2$ and $d_T=-4\pi c/(\omega^2-c^2q^2)$ (E Eq. 375). Since $P^LP^L=P^L$, $P^TP^T=P^T$ and $P^LP^T=0$, the series E Eq. 378 sums channel by channel, $D_{L,T}=d_{L,T}/(1-d_{L,T}\Pi_{L,T})$, which gives the forms in the text; no product contains $P^LP^T$, so $D^{lt}=D^{tl}=0$. With E Eq. 350, $\Pi_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{cq^2}{\omega^2}\Pi_L$, hence $1-v\Pi_{\rho\rho}=\epsilon_L$.

In $\bq$-space E Eq. 359 is $-\frac{c}{\omega^2}q_\mu q_\nu$, so $D^{ll}_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}q_\mu q_\nu D_{11}$. Comparing with $D^{ll}=D_LP^L$ gives $D_{11}=-\frac{\omega^2}{cq^2}D_L=\frac{4\pi}{q^2\epsilon_L}$.

For the polar model, $\epsilon=\epsilon_\infty(\omega_{LO}^2-\omega^2)/(\omega_{TO}^2-\omega^2)$, and $\omega^2\epsilon=c^2q^2$ is the quadratic $\epsilon_\infty\omega^4-(\epsilon_\infty\omega_{LO}^2+c^2q^2)\,\omega^2+c^2q^2\omega_{TO}^2=0$ with roots $\omega_\pm^2$. The same algebra with $\epsilon=(\omega_L^2-\omega^2)/(\Delta^2-\omega^2)$ gives the polaritons of the two-level insulator in the figure.

Bridge to Giustino: $W$ is the $ll$ sector of $D$

The scalar slot of EPP's propagator is Giustino's screened Coulomb interaction (§A.5). In an isotropic medium, exactly,

$$D^{ll}_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,q_\mu q_\nu\,W(\bq,\omega),\qquad W=D_{11}=\frac{4\pi}{q^2\,\epsilon_L(\bq,\omega)} .$$

Resumming only electronic bubbles gives Giustino's

$$W_{\rm e}(12)=v(12)+\int d(34)\,v(13)\,P_{\rm e}(34)\,W_{\rm e}(42),\tag{G.94}$$

with $P_{\rm e}\leftrightarrow\Pi^{\rm e}_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\bq\cdot\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj}\cdot\bq$. Adding the ions, $\epsilon_L=\epsilon_\infty-v\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}$ for the polar model, and expanding $1/\epsilon_L$ with $W_{\rm e}=4\pi/(q^2\epsilon_\infty)$:

$$W=W_{\rm e}+W_{\rm e}\,\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}\,W_{\rm e}+W_{\rm e}\,\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}\,W_{\rm e}\,\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}\,W_{\rm e}+\dots\equiv W_{\rm e}+W_{\rm e}\,\mathcal D\,W_{\rm e}.$$

This is $W=W_{\rm e}+W_{\rm ph}$ with $W_{\rm ph}=\int d(34)\,W_{\rm e}(13)\mathcal D(34)W_{\rm e}(24)$ (G Eqs. 104–105). Giustino's nuclear density correlator $\mathcal D$ (G Eq. 103) is represented by the Born-charge $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{\rho\rho}$ dressed by $W_{\rm e}$. Three things differ on EPP's side, one addition and two restrictions:

  • the vector block ($lt$, $tl$, $tt$), which carries transverse photons;
  • Born-charge point dipoles instead of bare nuclei with $\nabla V_\kappa$ (G Eq. 110), so only the long-range part of $\mathcal D$ is represented;
  • RPA without xc or local fields.

In an isotropic medium the $ll$ sector never sees $c$. Retardation in EPP's sense (finite speed of light) enters $W$ only through $l$–$t$ mixing, the diagrams of EPP Fig. 8: in anisotropic crystals off the principal axes, with local fields, and in 2D sheets (§B.10). The formal $c\to\infty$ statement is E Eqs. 437 and 441 (§B.9).

What the spectral map leaves out

The response is local. That is accurate here, since the plotted $q\lesssim10\,\omega/c$ is tiny on the scale of $k_F$ or the Brillouin zone; at larger $q$ plasmons disperse and $\Pi_L\neq\Pi_T$. The polar model uses a constant $\epsilon_\infty$ for the electrons. Uniaxial hBN mixes $L$ and $T$ off its axes, $\hat\bq\cdot\Pi_{jj}\cdot\hat{\mathbf t}\propto(\Pi_\parallel-\Pi_\perp)\sin\theta\cos\theta$. This mixing, with $\epsilon_\parallel$ and $\epsilon_\perp$ of opposite sign inside its Reststrahlen bands, produces its hyperbolic phonon polaritons, which the isotropic map cannot show. A 2D sheet needs the sheet propagator $D^0(\bQ,\omega;0,0)$, not just $\Omega\to S$ (§B.10).

Notes on the source

E Eq. 312 has the same number-versus-charge-density slip in $\rho^{\rm e}$ as E.235 (note in §B.4). E Eq. 314 is printed with $\sum_{i\nu}$; the atom index $a$ must be summed too, as written above. The scalar slot labelled "1" in $D_{11}$, $D_{1\nu}$, $D_{\mu1}$ is conventionally labelled 0. On p. 74, "$\Pi_{j\rho}$ is paired with $-\frac1c\int\bj\cdot\bA^{\rm ext}$" should read $\Pi_{\rho j}$, and in Fig. 10(c) "$j^{ie}$" should read $j^{\rm e}$. E Eq. 380 drops $\bG,\bG'$ without comment. The claim on p. 86 that "the transition to 2D case is trivial" is incomplete, as noted above.

With E Eq. 379 in hand, EPP turns the series around: §B.7 asks how light, screened by the electrons, dresses the lattice.

B.7EPP §7, §7.1 · Eqs. 386–410

The electrodynamic phonon self-energy and the LO–TO splitting

A polar phonon dresses itself by emitting and reabsorbing an electron-screened photon. By the end you can derive EPP's phonon Dyson equation, recognise it as Giustino's Eqs. (135) and (137) with photons, and explain why EPP's $\bq=0$ "LO–TO splitting" (E Eq. 410) is really the upper phonon polariton of a crystal without electrons.

In §B.6 the whole crystal was folded into one field propagator, $D=D^0+D^0\Pi_{jj}D$ with $\Pi_{jj}=\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj}+\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}$. EPP §7 reads the same diagram series the other way round. Instead of asking how matter dresses light, it asks how light dresses the lattice. Units are Gaussian throughout, and the Born charges $Z^*$ carry the dimension of charge.

Physical picture

A long-wavelength polar phonon is a lattice of identical oscillating Born-charge dipoles. An oscillating dipole is a current, $\dot{\bp}$, and a current radiates: it creates a longitudinal (Coulomb) field and a transverse photon field. That field crosses the polarizable electron gas, which screens it, and acts back on the ions. The loop phonon → current → screened field → current → phonon contains everything long-range in polar lattice dynamics: the LO–TO splitting, phonon polaritons and, in doped crystals, LO-phonon–plasmon modes. The bare frequencies $\omega_\sigma(\bq)$ keep only the short-range forces (§B.1).

Step 1: resum the electrons into the photon line

Take every diagram of $D$ that starts and ends on a bare ionic bubble and remove the outer $D^0$ lines. What remains is the screened ionic current–current correlator. From here on a superscript 0 marks a bare (irreducible) bubble (EPP p. 87). With the arguments $(\bq,\omega)$ written only in the first line,

$$\begin{aligned}\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)&=\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)+\sum_{\alpha\beta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)D^0_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\beta\nu}(\bq,\omega)\\&\quad+\sum_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\alpha}D^0_{\alpha\beta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\beta\gamma}D^0_{\gamma\delta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\delta\nu}+\sum_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\alpha}D^0_{\alpha\beta}\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\beta\gamma}D^0_{\gamma\delta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\delta\nu}+\dots\end{aligned}\tag{E.386}$$

Between two ionic bubbles any chain of electronic bubbles may appear. Collecting those chains into an electron-dressed photon line $D^{\rm e}$ leaves only ionic bubbles:

$$\begin{aligned}\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)&=\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)+\sum_{\alpha\beta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\beta\nu}(\bq,\omega)\\&\quad+\sum_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\alpha}D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\beta\gamma}D^{\rm e}_{\gamma\delta}\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\delta\nu}+\dots\end{aligned}\tag{E.387}$$
$$D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)+\sum_{\alpha\beta=xyz}D^0_{\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,D^{\rm e}_{\beta\nu}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.388}$$

E Eq. 388 is the Dyson equation of §B.6 with the electronic self-energy only. The author's analogy is the response of a medium A embedded in a polarizable medium B: $\chi_A=\chi^0_A+\chi^0_AW_B\chi^0_A+\dots$ with $W_B=v+v\chi^0_BW_B$. If you have screened a 2D layer by its substrate, this is the same move. The ions are system A, the electrons are the environment B, and $D^{\rm e}$ plays the role of $W_B$, now with transverse photons included.

Step 2: open the ionic bubble

The bare ionic bubble is a sum over the $3s$ bare phonon branches ($s$ atoms of mass $m_a$ per cell of volume $\Omega_{\rm uc}$, eigenvectors $e_{a\alpha\sigma}$). It is built from the ionic current vertex $j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)=\sum_{a\alpha}Z^*_{a\mu\alpha}e_{a\alpha\sigma}(\bq)/\sqrt{m_a}$ (E Eq. 295). The bare phonon propagator is the second line:

$$\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{\omega^2}{c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\frac{j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)\,j^*_{\nu\sigma}(\bq)}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}\tag{E.389}$$
$$F^0_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=2\,\frac{\omega_\sigma(\bq)}{\hbar}\,\frac{1}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+i\eta}\tag{E.390}$$

The bubble becomes "vertex × phonon line × vertex" once one defines the dynamical ionic current vertex:

$$j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)\;\to\;J_{\mu\sigma}(\bq,\omega)=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma(\bq)}}\;\omega\,j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)\tag{E.392}$$
$$\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}J_{\mu\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,F^0_\sigma(\bq,\omega)\,J^*_{\nu\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.393}$$

The factor $\omega$ is physical. A Born-charge dipole oscillating as $e^{-i\omega t}$ carries the current $\dot{\bp}=-i\omega\bp$, and the field couples to currents through $-\frac1c\bj\cdot\bA$. A static displacement carries no current, so $J(\omega=0)=0$. The two vertices carry the overall $\omega^2$ of the gauge-invariant bubble, which came from subtracting the static paramagnetic term (§B.5). The square root collects the zero-point amplitude $\sqrt{\hbar/2m_a\omega_\sigma}$ (the mass is already inside $j$) and the $1/\sqrt{c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}}$ normalization of the current coupling.

Step 3: a Dyson equation for phonons

Insert E Eq. 393 into E Eq. 387. Each bare ionic bubble becomes $-JF^0J^*$, and between two phonon lines sits the combination $J^*D^{\rm e}J$. Defining minus that combination as the phonon self-energy, the series reads (unnumbered, EPP p. 89)

$$\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj\mu\nu}=-\sum_{\sigma\sigma'}J_{\mu\sigma}\left\{F^0+F^0\Omega^{\rm e}F^0+F^0\Omega^{\rm e}F^0\Omega^{\rm e}F^0+\dots\right\}J^*_{\nu\sigma'},$$

and the curly bracket is the perturbative expansion of the phonon Green's matrix:

$$F=F^0+F^0\Omega^{\rm e}F^0+F^0\Omega^{\rm e}F^0\Omega^{\rm e}F^0+\dots\tag{E.397}$$
$$F=F^0+F^0\,\Omega^{\rm e}\,F\tag{E.398}$$
$$\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J_{\beta\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.399}$$
$\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}$

Diagrams after EPP Figs. 12–13. Amber zigzag: phonon ($F^0$ thin, $F$ heavy). Rose wavy: total photon line, longitudinal plus transverse ($D^0$ thin, $D^{\rm e}$ heavy). Blobs: bare ionic (amber) and electronic (blue) current–current bubbles. Teal dots: the dynamical ionic vertices $J$, $J^*$. In the phonon row, the piece $J^*$–$D^{\rm e}$–$J$ stands for $\Omega^{\rm e}$, including the minus sign of E Eq. 399.

Derivation: E Eq. 393 reproduces E Eq. 389, and the signs of the Dyson series

Insert E Eqs. 390 and 392:

$$-J_{\mu\sigma}F^0_\sigma J^*_{\nu\sigma}=-\frac{\hbar\,\omega^2}{2c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma}\,j_{\mu\sigma}j^*_{\nu\sigma}\cdot\frac{2\omega_\sigma}{\hbar}\,\frac{1}{\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2+i\eta}=-\frac{\omega^2}{c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}}\frac{j_{\mu\sigma}j^*_{\nu\sigma}}{\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2+i\eta}.$$

The term of E Eq. 387 with $n$ lines $D^{\rm e}$ contains $n+1$ bare bubbles, so $(-1)^{n+1}$ from E Eq. 393, and $n$ factors $J^*D^{\rm e}J=-\Omega^{\rm e}$, so another $(-1)^n$. The product is always $-1$: the term equals $-J\,F^0(\Omega^{\rm e}F^0)^n J^*$, which is the bracket above. Summing the geometric series gives E Eq. 398.

$\Omega^{\rm e}$ is a $3s\times3s$ matrix. Off-diagonal elements mix branches, because one photon line can connect two different polar modes. EPP splits it as $\Omega^{\rm e}=\Omega^0+\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}$ (E Eq. 400), with an electron-free part

$$\Omega^0_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,D^0_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J_{\beta\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.401}$$

and an electron-induced remainder $\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}$, where the electrodynamic Fröhlich vertices live (§B.8). Neglecting phonon mixing, $F_{\sigma\sigma'}\approx F_\sigma\delta_{\sigma\sigma'}$, E Eq. 398 becomes algebra:

$$F_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=\frac{F^0_\sigma(\bq,\omega)}{1-F^0_\sigma(\bq,\omega)\,\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}(\bq,\omega)}\tag{E.404}$$
$$F_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=\frac1\hbar\,\frac{2\omega_\sigma(\bq)}{\omega^2-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)-2\omega_\sigma(\bq)\,\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}(\bq,\omega)/\hbar}\tag{E.405}$$

The renormalized frequencies solve $\omega^2=\omega_\sigma^2+2\omega_\sigma\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}(\bq,\omega)/\hbar$, a self-consistent condition because $\Omega^{\rm e}$ depends on $\omega$. For the optical modes of a cubic diatomic crystal near $\Gamma$, choosing the bare modes along and across $\hat\bq$ makes $\Omega^{\rm e}$ diagonal among the optical modes. The acoustic modes carry no current at $\Gamma$, so E Eq. 404 is exact at $\Gamma$ and accurate near it. The figure below uses this.

Why the infinite sum matters. Each finite order of E Eq. 397 is a polynomial in $F^0$ and $\Omega^{\rm e}$. Its poles are those of $F^0$, at the bare $\omega_\sigma$ with growing multiplicity, plus any poles of $\Omega^{\rm e}$ itself, such as the bare photon. None of them is a renormalized mode. The geometric series converges only where $|F^0\Omega^{\rm e}|\lt 1$, and the renormalized pole sits exactly on the boundary, where $F^0\Omega^{\rm e}=1$. No truncation reaches it. The "Why resum?" tab of the figure shows this numerically.

Bridge to Giustino: the same Dyson equation

Here Giustino's phonon Green's function is written $\boldsymbol{\mathcal D}$ and his phonon self-energy $\Pi^{\rm ph}$ (in the PDF they are $\mathbf D$ and $\Pi$; see §A.6), with nonadiabatic part $\Pi^{\rm NA}=\Pi^{\rm ph}-\Pi^{\rm A}$. His adiabatic propagator $\mathcal D^{\rm A}_{\bq\nu\nu'}=2\omega_{\bq\nu}\delta_{\nu\nu'}/(\omega^2-\omega^2_{\bq\nu})$ (G Eq. 132) has the form of $\hbar F^0_\sigma$, with adiabatic frequencies in place of EPP's short-range ones. Giustino §V.A.2 writes

$$\boldsymbol{\mathcal D}(\omega)=\boldsymbol{\mathcal D}^{\rm A}(\omega)+\boldsymbol{\mathcal D}^{\rm A}(\omega)\,\Pi^{\rm NA}(\omega)\,\boldsymbol{\mathcal D}(\omega)\tag{G.135}$$
$$\tilde\Omega^2_{\bq\nu}=\omega^2_{\bq\nu}+2\omega_{\bq\nu}\,\Pi^{\rm NA}_{\bq\nu\nu}(\tilde\Omega_{\bq\nu})\tag{G.137}$$

These are E Eq. 398 and the pole condition of E Eq. 405, with $\Omega^{\rm e}/\hbar$ in the place of $\Pi^{\rm NA}$ (in general $\Omega^{\rm e}\leftrightarrow\hbar\,\Pi^{\rm ph}$): Giustino's self-energy is a frequency, EPP's an energy. Mind the letters: Giustino's $\tilde\Omega$ is a renormalized frequency, EPP's $\Omega^{\rm e}$ a self-energy and $\Omega_{\rm uc}$ a cell volume. Both papers drop the off-diagonal elements, Giustino's effect (iii) "coupling between the adiabatic vibrational eigenmodes", and both solve the pole condition self-consistently (E Eq. 407 below). The theories differ in what they call the unperturbed phonon:

Giustino (2017)EPP §7
Unperturbed phononsadiabatic: DFPT force constants $\Pi^{\rm A}=\Pi^{\rm ph}(\omega=0)$, long-range dipolar part includedshort-range force constants only; the dipolar part is removed
Self-energy$\Pi^{\rm NA}$: dynamic minus static, $W_{\rm e}(\omega)-W_{\rm e}(0)$ (G Eq. 140)$\Omega^{\rm e}=-J^*D^{\rm e}J$: the whole long-range part, static and dynamic
Field exchangedinstantaneous Coulomb, screened by $\epsilon_{\rm e}^{-1}$longitudinal and transverse photons, screened by $D^{\rm e}$
Chargesbare nuclear $Z_\kappa$Born charges $Z^*$, point dipoles at cell origins

So $\Omega^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$, which is purely longitudinal (at $\omega=0$ the $\omega^2$ of $J^*J$ cancels the $1/\omega^2$ of the longitudinal $D^{\rm e}$ and removes the transverse part), is the long-range part of Giustino's $\Pi^{\rm A}$. $\Omega^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)-\Omega^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$ is the dipolar part of his $\Pi^{\rm NA}$, plus the transverse-photon part that his theory does not have.

§7.1: switch the electrons off and set q = 0

With $D^{\rm e}\to D^0$ the self-energy is E Eq. 401 on the diagonal, and the pole condition must be solved self-consistently:

$$\Omega^0_\sigma(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,D^0_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J_{\beta\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.406}$$
$$\tilde\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)=\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+2\omega_\sigma(\bq)\,\Omega^0_{\sigma\sigma}\big[\bq,\tilde\omega_\sigma(\bq)\big]/\hbar\tag{E.407}$$

The free propagator of §B.6,

$$D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\,\frac{-q_\mu q_\nu+\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}\delta_{\mu\nu}}{q^2-\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}-i\eta},\tag{E.381}$$

loses its direction dependence in the optical limit $\bq=0$:

$$D^0_{\alpha\beta}(\bq=0,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\,\delta_{\alpha\beta}\tag{E.408}$$

The $\omega^2$ in $J^*J$ cancels the $1/\omega^2$ of $D^0$. The self-energy is frequency independent, and the self-consistency becomes trivial:

$$\Omega^0_{\sigma\sigma}(\bq=0)=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{\Omega_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma(\bq=0)}\sum_\alpha\big|j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq=0)\big|^2\tag{E.409}$$
$$\tilde\omega^2_\sigma(\bq=0)=\omega^2_\sigma(\bq=0)+\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_\alpha\big|j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq=0)\big|^2\tag{E.410}$$

For a cubic diatomic crystal ($Z^*_a=-Z^*_b=Z^*$, reduced mass $\mu$) every polar optical mode has $\sum_\alpha|j_{\alpha\sigma}|^2=Z^{*2}/\mu$. The shift is then the ionic plasma frequency of §B.3, $\omega_p^2=4\pi Z^{*2}/(\Omega_{\rm uc}\mu)$. Note the size of E Eq. 409: for GaAs ($Z^*=2.07$, $\hbar\omega_\sigma=33.3$ meV; literature values, illustrative) it is about 30 meV (33 meV in the figure, whose $\omega_p$ comes from the measured splitting), comparable to $\hbar\omega_\sigma$ itself. There is no small parameter, which is why the resummation matters.

Derivation: from E Eq. 406 to E Eq. 410, and the same at finite q

With E Eq. 392, $\Omega^0_{\sigma\sigma}=-\frac{\hbar\omega^2}{2c\Omega_{\rm uc}\omega_\sigma}\sum_{\alpha\beta}j^*_{\alpha\sigma}D^0_{\alpha\beta}j_{\beta\sigma}$. At $\bq=0$, E Eq. 408 gives $\frac{\hbar\omega^2}{2c\Omega_{\rm uc}\omega_\sigma}\cdot\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\sum_\alpha|j_{\alpha\sigma}|^2$, which is E Eq. 409. Then $2\omega_\sigma\Omega^0_{\sigma\sigma}/\hbar=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_\alpha|j_{\alpha\sigma}|^2$, and E Eq. 407 becomes E Eq. 410.

At finite $\bq$, project E Eq. 381 on $\hat\bq$ and on a unit vector $\hat{\mathbf t}\perp\bq$. The mixed elements vanish and

$$\hat\bq\cdot D^0\cdot\hat\bq=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2},\qquad \hat{\mathbf t}\cdot D^0\cdot\hat{\mathbf t}=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2-c^2q^2}.$$

Split $\bj_\sigma=\bj_{\sigma\parallel}+\bj_{\sigma\perp}$ and write $\omega^2_{p\parallel,\perp}=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}|\bj_{\sigma\parallel,\perp}|^2$. Then $2\omega_\sigma\Omega^0_{\sigma\sigma}/\hbar=\omega^2_{p\parallel}+\omega^2_{p\perp}\,\omega^2/(\omega^2-c^2q^2)$, which gives the finite-$q$ condition in the text.

Electrons below the gap of an insulator can be modelled by $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\mu\nu}=\frac{(\epsilon_\infty-1)\omega^2}{4\pi c}\delta_{\mu\nu}$, the small-$\omega$ form of the electronic bubble (§B.5). E Eq. 388 then gives $\hat\bq\cdot D^{\rm e}\cdot\hat\bq=-\frac{4\pi c}{\epsilon_\infty\omega^2}$ and $\hat{\mathbf t}\cdot D^{\rm e}\cdot\hat{\mathbf t}=-\frac{4\pi c}{\epsilon_\infty\omega^2-c^2q^2}$. For the transverse modes of a cubic diatomic crystal, the poles of E Eq. 405 then satisfy $(\omega^2-\omega_\sigma^2)(\epsilon_\infty\omega^2-c^2q^2)=\omega_p^2\omega^2$, whose roots are

$$\omega_\pm^2=\frac{(\epsilon_\infty\omega_L^2+c^2q^2)\pm\sqrt{(\epsilon_\infty\omega_L^2+c^2q^2)^2-4\epsilon_\infty c^2q^2\omega_\sigma^2}}{2\epsilon_\infty},\qquad \omega_L^2=\omega_\sigma^2+\frac{\omega_p^2}{\epsilon_\infty}.$$

The residue of $F_\sigma$ at each pole in the variable $\omega^2$, relative to the bare residue $2\omega_\sigma/\hbar$, is the phonon weight $Z_\pm=\big[1+\omega_p^2c^2q^2/(\epsilon_\infty\omega_\pm^2-c^2q^2)^2\big]^{-1}$, and $Z_++Z_-=1$.

What E Eq. 410 is, and what it is not

EPP opens §7.1 with "This procedure is completely analogous to the non-analytic dynamical matrix correction done by Quantum Espresso." The analogy holds in form: both shifts are built from Born charges and the cell volume. But E Eq. 410 is a different limit, and it is not the LO–TO splitting that DFPT adds. Three features give it away.

  • It is isotropic. $\sum_\alpha|j_{\alpha\sigma}|^2$ counts all three components of the mode current. At $\bq=0$ the two transverse modes shift exactly as much as the longitudinal one. The DFPT non-analytic term depends on $|\hat\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2$ and leaves TO modes where they are.
  • It is unscreened. No electrons means $\epsilon_\infty=1$. For GaAs ($Z^*\approx2.07$, $\Omega_{\rm uc}=a^3/4=45.2$ Å$^3$, $\mu=36.1$ amu, $\hbar\omega_{\rm TO}=33.3$ meV, $\hbar\omega_{\rm LO}=36.2$ meV; literature values, illustrative) and Gaussian $e^2=14.40$ eV Å, $\hbar\omega_p\approx44.6$ meV. E Eq. 410 then puts the shifted mode at $\sqrt{33.3^2+44.6^2}\approx56$ meV, against the measured LO phonon at 36.2 meV. The electrons divide the shift by $\epsilon_\infty\approx10.9$, and that factor only arrives with $\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}$ (§B.8).
  • It is retarded, in EPP's sense of a finite speed of light (not Giustino's sense of frequency-dependent screening). E Eq. 408 is the regime $cq\ll\omega$, inside the light cone. There the shifted "phonon" is the $\bq=0$ end of the upper phonon polariton.

Keeping $\bq$ finite shows all three at once. With $\bj_\sigma$ split along and across $\hat\bq$, E Eqs. 381, 392 and 406 give (derived here, not in the manuscript)

$$\omega^2=\omega_\sigma^2+\omega_{p\parallel}^2+\omega_{p\perp}^2\,\frac{\omega^2}{\omega^2-c^2q^2},\qquad \omega^2_{p\parallel,\perp}=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\,|\bj_{\sigma\parallel,\perp}|^2 .$$

The longitudinal part never sees $c$: $\hat\bq\cdot D^0\cdot\hat\bq=-4\pi c/\omega^2$ at every $q$, so the LO mode sits at $\sqrt{\omega_\sigma^2+\omega_{p\parallel}^2}$ for all $q$. The transverse part is the polariton condition $c^2q^2=\omega^2\epsilon(\omega)$ with $\epsilon(\omega)=1+\omega_p^2/(\omega_\sigma^2-\omega^2)$, the photon-side picture of §B.6 seen from the phonon. Its upper branch starts at $\sqrt{\omega_\sigma^2+\omega_p^2}$ at $q=0$, which is E Eq. 410, while the lower branch is photon-like there. Electrons, modelled by a constant $\epsilon_\infty$, divide $\omega_{p\parallel}^2$ by $\epsilon_\infty$ and turn $\omega^2-c^2q^2$ into $\epsilon_\infty\omega^2-c^2q^2$.

The order of limits

In this result $c$ and $q$ enter only through the product $cq$. The limits $q\to0$ and $c\to\infty$ therefore do not commute:

  • $q\to0$ at fixed $c$ (E Eq. 410; with electrons, $\omega_p^2\to\omega_p^2/\epsilon_\infty$): all three polar modes sit at $\omega_L$, whatever the direction of approach. The transverse ones are the upper polariton.
  • $c\to\infty$ at fixed $q$, then $q\to0$ (E Eq. 454, §B.9): only the $ll$ sector of $D^{\rm e}$ survives, the TO modes stay at $\omega_\sigma$, and the LO shift carries $|\hat\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2/(\hat\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\hat\bq)$. This is the non-analytic LO–TO splitting of DFPT.

A real crystal has one value of $c$, and the crossover sits at the light-cone wave vector of §X.1, $q_c=\sqrt{\epsilon_\infty}\,\omega/c$ evaluated at $\omega_\sigma$, about $5.6\times10^{-5}$ Å$^{-1}$ in GaAs, or $5\times10^{-5}$ of $2\pi/a$. Taking $c\to\infty$ first is the right description of essentially the whole Brillouin zone, which is why electrostatic DFPT works. The limit behind E Eq. 410 takes $q\to0$ at finite $c$ and describes the tiny region on the other side of $q_c$, the region that optics probes. §X.1 makes the same argument from the propagator side.

What the model leaves out

The figure keeps the electrons static, a constant $\epsilon_\infty$. That is the adiabatic approximation for electronic screening and is fine in a gapped crystal. With free carriers, $\Pi^{\rm e,0}$ acquires a Drude term, $D^{\rm e}$ acquires a plasmon pole near phonon energies, and the dynamical $D^{\rm e}$ gives coupled LO-phonon–plasmon modes (§B.9). The Dyson route has no Lorentz local field, unlike the classical model of §B.3, so TO equals the bare $\omega_\sigma$. hBN is uniaxial; using one $\epsilon_\infty$ is a simplification. Real polaritons also carry damping, which only the second tab includes.

Bridge to Giustino: where his LO–TO splitting lives

Giustino's theory has only the instantaneous Coulomb interaction, so it lives in the $\lambda_c\to\infty$ limit of the figure. His LO–TO splitting sits inside the adiabatic force constants $\Pi^{\rm A}$, as the Gonze–Lee non-analytic term with $Z^*$ and $\epsilon^\infty$ that he cites in §VI.A.3 (§A.4). EPP derives that term as a self-energy (E Eq. 454) and adds what electrostatics cannot see: phonon polaritons for $q\lesssim q_c$, and an isotropic $\bq=0$ limit.

Note on the source

Wording and index slips in EPP §7.1 (E Eq. 391 should carry the superscript 0; "photon" stands for "phonon" before E Eqs. 406–407) are listed in Z.2. The Quantum Espresso comparison that opens §7.1 holds only for a mode polarized along $\hat\bq$ with $\epsilon_\infty=1$ (see above). EPP's propagators are time-ordered; the figure uses the retarded form with $i\eta\omega$ given on p. 88.

B.8EPP §7.2 · Eqs. 411–432

The electrodynamic Fröhlich vertex

Open the electron loop inside the phonon self-energy and an electron–phonon vertex appears that nobody put in by hand: one photon exchanged between an ionic and an electronic current. It depends on frequency, it comes in a bare and a screened version, and for $c\to\infty$ the screened one becomes the Verdi–Giustino vertex with $\epsilon^\infty$ replaced by the dynamical RPA tensor $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$.

A vertex made of a photon

In Giustino's Hamiltonian (G Eq. 1) the coupling $g_{mn\nu}(\bk,\bq)$ is an input: the matrix element of a screened potential change (G Eq. 38). The EPP Lagrangian has no such term (§B.2). Electrons couple to the vector potential through $\frac ec\mathbf v\cdot\bA$, ions through the polarization current of their Born-charge dipoles, $\frac1c\dot\bp\cdot\bA$. An electron can feel a phonon only by exchanging a photon with it, so the electron–phonon vertex is a composite: ionic current vertex, photon propagator, electronic current vertex. Only the long-range polar channel arises this way; the short-range deformation-potential part of Giustino's $g$ has no counterpart in the EPP Lagrangian (E.134).

§B.7 summed these exchanges into the phonon self-energy $\Omega^{\rm e}=-J^*D^{\rm e}J$ (E.399) and split it into an electron-free part $\Omega^0$ and an electron-induced part $\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}$ (E.400–402); this section opens $\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}$. Notation as in the rest of Part B: $D^0$ is the free photon propagator (E.375), $D^{\rm e}$ the one dressed by electrons only (E.388), $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj}$ and $\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj}$ the irreducible and reducible electronic photon self-energies, and $J_{\mu\sigma}(\bq,\omega)=\sqrt{\hbar/2c\Omega_{\rm uc}\omega_\sigma(\bq)}\;\omega\,j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)$ the ionic current vertex (E.392), built from the mode current $j_{\mu\sigma}(\bq)=\sum_{a\nu}Z^*_{a\mu\nu}e_{a\nu\sigma}(\bq)/\sqrt{m_a}$ (E.295) with atomic masses $m_a$ and phonon eigenvectors $e_{a\nu\sigma}$. Numbers use $e^2/\varepsilon_0=180.95$ eV Å.

Physical picture

A polar phonon is an oscillating dipole $\bp=Z^*\bQ$, that is, a current $\dot\bp=-i\omega\bp$, and a current radiates. The longitudinal part of its field is the Coulomb potential of a polarization wave; the transverse part is light. An electron absorbs the field through a transition $n\bk\to m\bk+\bq$, which also carries a current. Both ends bring a factor $\omega$ and the propagator knows the speed of light, so the vertex depends on frequency and on $c$, unlike the adiabatic $g(\bk,\bq)$.

Opening the electron bubble

The electron-induced self-energy contains the reducible electronic correlator between two bare photon lines:

$$\begin{aligned}\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}\sum_{\alpha_1\beta_1}&J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,D^0_{\alpha\alpha_1}(\bq,\omega)\,\Pi^{\rm e}_{jj\alpha_1\beta_1}(\bq,\omega)\\&\times D^0_{\beta_1\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J_{\beta\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)\end{aligned}\tag{E.411}$$

Expanding $\Pi^{\rm e}=\Pi^{\rm e,0}+\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}+\dots$ and regrouping the chain onto the left photon line gives

$$\begin{aligned}\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}\sum_{\alpha_1\beta_1}&J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\alpha_1}(\bq,\omega)\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\alpha_1\beta_1}(\bq,\omega)\\&\times D^0_{\beta_1\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J_{\beta\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)\end{aligned}\tag{E.412}$$

One photon line is now screened, the other bare, and the electronic bubble between them is irreducible.

Derivation: from (E.411) to (E.412)

Suppress the Cartesian indices; every product is a $3\times3$ matrix product at fixed $(\bq,\omega)$:

$$\begin{aligned}D^0\Pi^{\rm e}D^0&=D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0+D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0+\dots\\&=\big(D^0+D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0+\dots\big)\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0=D^{\rm e}\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0,\end{aligned}$$

using the Dyson series of $D^{\rm e}$ (E.388). Nothing is approximated: the same chain of bubbles is read from a different end.

Inserting the RPA current correlator (E.383, §B.5) and splitting each transition into vertex × propagator × vertex defines the dynamical electron current vertex and the bare electron–hole propagator; the latter is boxed but unnumbered on EPP p. 92:

$$J^\mu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\omega)=\sqrt{\frac{1}{c\Omega}}\;\frac{\hbar\omega}{E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}}\;j^\mu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}\tag{E.414}$$
$$\chi^0_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\omega)=2\,\frac{E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}}{\hbar\omega}\;\frac{f_{n\bk}-f_{m\bk+\bq}}{\hbar\omega+E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}+i\eta}$$

Here $E_{n\bk}$ and $f_{n\bk}$ are band energies and occupations, $\Omega=N\Omega_{\rm uc}$ is the crystal volume ($N$ cells), $j^\mu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}$ is the paramagnetic current matrix element of E.384 (it contains $e$), and the 2 counts spin. The product $J^\mu\chi^0[J^\nu]^*$ reproduces the summand of E.383 exactly.

Do not implement $J^{\rm e}$ and $\chi^0$ separately

EPP's $\chi^0$ is not the Lindhard function.
