With $\Delta E=E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}$ and $\Delta E/[\hbar\omega(\hbar\omega+\Delta E)]=1/\hbar\omega-1/(\hbar\omega+\Delta E)$ it splits into the familiar density bubble plus a term $\propto(f_{n\bk}-f_{m\bk+\bq})/\hbar\omega$ that cancels only for a complete band sum (longitudinally it is $\sum(f_{n\bk}-f_{m\bk+\bq})|\rho_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}|^2=0$). The vertex $J^{\rm e}\propto1/\Delta E$ diverges for intraband transitions as $q\to0$ and for degenerate bands; only the product $J^{\rm e}\chi^0J^{\rm e*}$ is regular. In a truncated-band code use E.383 directly or, longitudinally, the charge vertices of (cf. E.428).

Two vertices, one bubble

Grouping each photon line with the two current vertices at its ends defines the bare and the screened electrodynamic electron–phonon vertices,

$$g^{\rm dyn,0}_{nm\sigma}(\bk,\bq,\omega)=i\sum_{\alpha\beta=xyz}\big[J^\alpha_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\omega)\big]^*\,D^0_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J_{\beta\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.415}$$
$$g^{\rm dyn}_{nm\sigma}(\bk,\bq,\omega)=i\sum_{\alpha\beta=xyz}J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq,\omega)\,D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,J^\beta_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\omega)\tag{E.416}$$

and the electron-induced self-energy takes the shape of Giustino's phonon self-energy, vertex × bubble × vertex (EPP p. 92, unnumbered):

$$\Delta\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bq,\omega)=\sum_{\bk\in{\rm BZ},nm}g^{\rm dyn}_{nm\sigma}(\bk,\bq,\omega)\;\chi^0_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\omega)\;g^{\rm dyn,0}_{nm\sigma'}(\bk,\bq,\omega)$$

The two factors of $i$ supply the minus sign of E.412–413. Read from left to right (EPP Fig. 14): phonon $\sigma$ emits through its Born-charge current $J^*$; the photon crosses the polarizable electrons ($D^{\rm e}$, longitudinal and transverse); an electron makes the transition $n\bk\to m\bk+\bq$ ($\chi^0$); the pair recombines into a bare photon ($D^0$), which phonon $\sigma'$ absorbs.

Why only one dressed line? Write $x=D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}$ for one electronic bubble hung on a bare line (schematically, as a scalar). Then $D^0\Pi^{\rm e}D^0=D^0(x+x^2+x^3+\dots)$ contains every chain of $k$ bubbles exactly once. Dressing both lines gives $D^{\rm e}\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^{\rm e}=D^0x/(1-x)^2$, that is $D^0(x+2x^2+3x^3+\dots)$, which contains the $k$-bubble chain $k$ times: double counting. Leaving both lines bare, $D^0\Pi^{\rm e,0}D^0=D^0x$, keeps only the one-bubble term: screening to first order, never resummed (derived here, not printed in EPP; steps of this kind are marked [derived] below). The correct count is either two bare lines around the reducible $\Pi^{\rm e}$ (E.411) or one bare and one screened line around the irreducible $\Pi^{\rm e,0}$ (E.412). In the static long-wavelength limit of an insulator, $1-x$ is the electronic dielectric constant $\epsilon$ (E.432), so the three pairings multiply the bare dipolar shift $\Omega^0$ by $1+(1/\epsilon-1)$, $1+(1-\epsilon)/\epsilon^2$ and $1+(1-\epsilon)$. The figure turns these factors into LO frequencies.

Bridge to Giustino: one bare vertex, one screened

Giustino's nonperturbative phonon self-energy (G §V.A.3, see §A.6) has the same structure, (G.141): the bare coupling $g^{\rm b}=\Delta_{\bq\nu}V^{\rm en}$ (G Eq. 142) at one end, the dynamically screened $g^{\rm cc}=\epsilon_{\rm e}^{-1}g^{\rm b,*}$ (G Eq. 144) at the other, and the irreducible $P_{\rm e}$ between them. $g^{\rm dyn,0}$ and $g^{\rm dyn}$ are their electrodynamic, long-range counterparts, and $D^{\rm e}=(\hat\epsilon^{\rm e})^{-1}D^0$ (E.431) mirrors $g=\epsilon_{\rm e}^{-1}g^{\rm b}$ (G Eq. 143). Two differences: EPP needs no static subtraction, because its bare phonons hold only short-range forces, and it keeps the $\omega$ dependence of the screened vertex, which Giustino drops in his approximation (iv) on the way to (G.145). Giustino notes that most ab initio calculations replace $g^{\rm b}$ by $g$ in (G.145), for nonadiabatic frequencies as well as in the lifetime formula (G.146), and asks for the effect of the bare vertex to be tested (G §V.A.3, p. 015003-25). For the real part, the frequency shift, the replacement is the miscount of the "two screened" curve above, applied to the nonadiabatic part; for the width it is harmless in a consistent RPA as long as $\epsilon(\omega_{\bq\nu})\approx\epsilon(0)$ (§A.6).

Which vertex is screened, and at which frequency

"One bare, one screened" holds for self-energies with an electron bubble between the vertices; Fan–Migdal, with no bubble there, has two screened vertices (§A.7). The pairing is exact, but freezing the screened vertex at $\omega=0$, as (G.145) does, overestimates linewidths by about $\epsilon(\bq,0)$ in metals (§A.6). EPP keeps the dynamic form through $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$.

From currents to charges: the continuity identity

To compare with the electrostatic vertices of Part A, the current vertex has to become a charge vertex. EPP evolves the density and current operators with the band Hamiltonian $H^{\rm e}_0=\sum_{n\bk}E_{n\bk}c^+_{n\bk}c_{n\bk}$ (E.421), imposes continuity $\dot\rho_{\rm e}=-\nabla\cdot\bj_{\rm e}$ (E.422), Fourier transforms and compares coefficients (E.423–427). With the charge restored on the left (see the note below), and with the charge vertex $\rho_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}=\langle\phi_{n\bk}|e^{-i\bq\cdot\br}|\phi_{m\bk+\bq}\rangle$ (E.106 at $\bG=0$):

$$e\,\rho_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}=-\sum_\mu\hbar q_\mu\,\frac{j^\mu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}}{E_{n\bk}-E_{m\bk+\bq}}\tag{cf. E.428}$$

This is $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot\bj=0$ for a single transition: $\bq\cdot\bj=\omega_{\rm tr}\,e\rho$ with $\omega_{\rm tr}=(E_{m\bk+\bq}-E_{n\bk})/\hbar$. For the dynamical vertex it gives $\sum_\mu q_\mu J^\mu_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}(\omega)=-\sqrt{1/c\Omega}\;\omega\,e\rho_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}$ [derived]: the longitudinal part of the electron current vertex is $\omega$ times the charge vertex, and the singular $1/\Delta E$ disappears.

Familiar from optics codes

This is the identity behind the equivalence of velocity- and length-gauge dipoles in RPA and BSE codes, $\langle v|\mathbf p|c\rangle=im\,\omega_{vc}\langle v|\br|c\rangle$ with $\omega_{vc}=(E_v-E_c)/\hbar$, with the same fine print: it holds for a local band Hamiltonian, and nonlocal pseudopotentials or scissor-shifted energies add commutator terms.

Note on the source: the missing $e^2$

As printed, E.428 equates the number-density vertex $\rho$ (E.106, E.420) with $-\hbar\bq\cdot\bj/\Delta E$, while $j^\mu$ (E.384) contains $e$. A free-electron check, $\phi=e^{i\bk\cdot\br}/\sqrt\Omega$, gives $-\hbar\bq\cdot\bj/\Delta E=e$, not 1, so the left side must read $e\rho$. The author saw the symptom; a blue margin note in Croatian (p. 96) reads "U odnosu na Giustino-a fali ti taj $e^2$. Vjerojatno je u interakciji D ili u $Z^*$…", that is, "Compared with Giustino you are missing that $e^2$. It is probably in the interaction D or in $Z^*$. Also, his notation for this matrix element is $g^0_{mn\sigma}$ and ours $g^0_{nm\sigma}$, but that is irrelevant." Resolution: one $e$ sits in EPP's charge-dimensioned Born charge ($Z^*_{\rm EPP}=|e|Z^*_{\rm G}$), the other is the one missing from E.428; $D$ is innocent. The p. 95 and p. 98 vertices below are shown as printed and acquire this $e$. Three smaller slips: the text before E.418 calls $c\to\infty$ the "retarded limit" (it is the instantaneous, non-retarded limit); the text before E.417 says the bare vertex reduces to E.131, which holds only with $\epsilon^\infty=1$ and $\bG=0$ (as p. 96 then concedes); and the Heisenberg evolution on p. 93 lacks $\hbar$ in the exponent.

The electrostatic limit: Verdi–Giustino with $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$

The Dyson equation for $D^{\rm e}$ (E.388) can be written as a dielectric problem,

$$\sum_\alpha\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)\,D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\nu}(\bq,\omega)=D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.431}$$
$$\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=\delta_{\mu\nu}-\sum_\alpha D^0_{\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\alpha\nu}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.432}$$

As $c\to\infty$ only the longitudinal sector survives (derivation in §B.9), and $D^{\rm e}$ becomes the screened Coulomb interaction in vector form:

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\,\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{\sum_{\alpha\beta}q_\alpha\,\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,q_\beta}\tag{E.446}$$

Inserting E.375 and E.446 into the two vertices and using E.428 gives (EPP pp. 95 and 98, unnumbered, as printed):

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}g^{\rm dyn,0}_{nm\sigma}(\bk,\bq,\omega)=\frac{4\pi i}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_a\sum_{\mu\nu=xyz}\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2Nm_a\omega_\sigma(\bq)}}\;\frac{q_\mu Z^*_{a\mu\nu}\,e_{a\nu\sigma}(\bq)}{q^2}\;\big[\rho_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}\big]^*$$
$$\lim_{c\to\infty}g^{\rm dyn}_{nm\sigma}(\bk,\bq,\omega)=\frac{4\pi i}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\sum_a\sum_{\mu\nu=xyz}\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2Nm_a\omega_\sigma(\bq)}}\;\frac{q_\mu Z^*_{a\mu\nu}\,e^*_{a\nu\sigma}(\bq)}{\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)\cdot\bq}\;\rho_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}$$

Compare with the Verdi–Giustino long-range vertex (G Eq. 180, §A.4), $\propto(\bq+\bG)\cdot\bZ^*_\kappa\cdot\be_{\kappa\nu}/[(\bq+\bG)\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon^\infty\cdot(\bq+\bG)]$ times a plane-wave matrix element. The bare vertex is Verdi–Giustino with $\epsilon^\infty=1$ and $\bG=0$. The screened vertex is Verdi–Giustino with $\epsilon^\infty$ replaced by $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$: the RPA tensor at the frequency at which the vertex is used, so the screening is nonadiabatic. This closes a loop opened in §B.1, where $\epsilon^\infty$ was put into the dipole potential by hand (EPP p. 23, E.112–120: "later we will remove it"); here it is generated by $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj}$. EPP calls the screened result "the conjugated complex part" of the vertex; comparing the two boxes makes this precise [derived]:

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}g^{\rm dyn}_{nm\sigma}=-\big[g^{\rm dyn,0}_{nm\sigma}\big]^*\,\frac{q^2}{\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)\cdot\bq},\qquad \Delta\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}\to-\frac{q^2}{\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}\cdot\bq}\sum_{\bk nm}\big|g^{\rm dyn,0}_{nm\sigma}\big|^2\chi^0_{n\bk,m\bk+\bq}$$

The electronic correction is minus the bare vertex squared, times the bubble, times the screening factor. For an insulator it is negative: the electrons soften the bare dipolar stiffening $\Omega^0$, as they must.

What "almost identical" hides

  • No local fields and no exchange–correlation: the screening is the head of the RPA dielectric matrix, not DFPT's macroscopic $\epsilon^\infty$ (§B.9).
  • The basis phase of G Eq. 180 is missing (source note in §B.1).
  • The zero-point amplitude contains the bare short-range $\omega_\sigma$, which is TO-like for a polar mode, whereas Verdi–Giustino use the physical $\omega_{\bq\nu}$. When $\Omega^{\rm e}$ is frequency independent, the phonon Dyson equation (E.405) gives the LO pole a quasiparticle weight $\omega_\sigma/\omega_{\rm LO}$, which turns $|g|^2\propto1/\omega_\sigma$ into $1/\omega_{\rm LO}$ [derived] (derivation in §X.2).

Nonadiabaticity matters when electrons can respond at the phonon frequency. In an undoped semiconductor the gap lies far above $\hbar\omega_{\rm LO}$, so $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega_{\rm LO})\approx\epsilon^\infty$ and static Verdi–Giustino screening is accurate. With free carriers it is not.

Across the light line: LO is Coulomb, TO needs photons

At finite $c$ the vertices contain the full propagator. Contracting E.375 with an ionic current along $\hat\bq$ (an LO mode in a cubic crystal) or perpendicular to it (TO) separates the two cases cleanly. Normalize each contraction $K$ by the bare Coulomb value $-4\pi c/\omega^2$.

Derivation: LO and TO kernels from (E.375)

The free propagator of the total field is

$$D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\,\frac{-q_\mu q_\nu+\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}\delta_{\mu\nu}}{q^2-\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}-i\eta}\tag{E.375}$$

For a unit vector $\hat{\mathbf t}\perp\bq$ [derived]:

$$\hat q_\mu D^0_{\mu\nu}\hat q_\nu=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2},\qquad \hat t_\mu D^0_{\mu\nu}\hat t_\nu=\frac{4\pi}{c}\,\frac{1}{q^2-\omega^2/c^2-i\eta},\qquad \hat q_\mu D^0_{\mu\nu}\hat t_\nu=0 .$$

So $K^0_{\rm LO}=1$ and $K^0_{\rm TO}=\omega^2/(\omega^2-c^2q^2)$. For electrons with a constant isotropic dielectric constant $\epsilon$, take $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj,\mu\nu}=(\epsilon-1)\,\omega^2\delta_{\mu\nu}/4\pi c$, which makes the longitudinal part of E.432 equal to $\epsilon$. Solving E.388 gives $K_{\rm LO}=1/\epsilon$ and $K_{\rm TO}=\omega^2/(\epsilon\omega^2-c^2q^2)=\epsilon^{-1}\,[1-(q/q_c)^2]^{-1}$ with $q_c=\sqrt\epsilon\,\omega/c$. For an LO current, $D^0\cdot\hat\bq=-(4\pi c/\omega^2)\hat\bq$ picks out $\hat\bq\cdot J^{\rm e*}$, and the corollary of (cf. E.428) turns E.415 into the p. 95 form at every $q$, not only for $c\to\infty$.

The LO kernel contains no $c$: longitudinal photons are the instantaneous Coulomb field at every $q$, so the $c\to\infty$ form of the LO vertex is exact, inside the light cone too. The TO kernel equals the LO one deep inside the light cone, resonates at the light line of the electronic medium, $q_c=\sqrt{\epsilon^\infty}\,\omega/c$ (the light-cone wave vector of §X.1), and decays as $(q_c/q)^2$ outside. TO phonons therefore couple to electrons, through transverse electronic currents, only inside or near the light cone, $q\lesssim q_c$. For GaAs $q_c\approx6\times10^{-5}$ Å$^{-1}$, four orders of magnitude below the zone boundary: invisible on the k-grids of transport calculations, central in optics, where it becomes the phonon-polariton physics of §B.7.

When the LO/TO split is clean

The clean split needs $\bj_\sigma$ purely along or across $\hat\bq$ and an isotropic $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}$; otherwise both kernels contribute. Also, at finite $c$ the transverse part of E.432 is not the optical dielectric function: for a constant electronic $\epsilon$ it equals $(q^2-\epsilon\omega^2/c^2)/(q^2-\omega^2/c^2)$ [derived], which tends to 1 as $c\to\infty$. Only the longitudinal part enters E.445–446.

In short, EPP derives the polar electron–phonon vertex instead of postulating it. Its static electrostatic limit is the Verdi–Giustino vertex; the additions are frequency-dependent RPA screening, bare/screened bookkeeping that cannot double count, and a photon-mediated coupling of TO phonons near the light cone. §B.9 takes $c\to\infty$ in the whole self-energy and recovers Giustino's LO–TO splitting.

B.9EPP §7.3 · Eqs. 433–454

The electrostatic limit: recovering Giustino

Let the speed of light go to infinity and EPP's electron-dressed photon keeps only its longitudinal–longitudinal sector, the RPA screened Coulomb interaction $W^{\rm e}$, which is the $W$ of GW without local fields. The phonon self-energy becomes proportional to $W^{\rm e}|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2$. At zero frequency it is the Gonze–Lee LO–TO term of DFPT; at the phonon frequency it produces the LO-phonon–plasmon modes that an adiabatic theory misses.

Part A never needed the speed of light. Giustino's interactions are the instantaneous Coulomb potential $v(\br-\br')\delta(t-t')$, dressed by the electrons into $W_{\rm e}$, and his LO–TO splitting and Fröhlich vertex are electrostatics with $Z^*$ and $\epsilon^\infty$ (§A.4, §A.5). EPP keeps $c$ finite, so $c\to\infty$ is a test it has to pass: the electrodynamic phonon self-energy of §B.7 must collapse onto Giustino's formulas. EPP §7.3 shows that it does, and the way it collapses is worth following step by step.

Units are Gaussian, with Born charges $Z^*$ that carry the dimension of charge (§B.1). In this section "retardation" always means EPP's finite speed of light. Giustino's sense of the word, frequency-dependent electronic screening, is called dynamic screening here.

Physical picture: what $c\to\infty$ removes

The transverse field is the part that has to travel: its propagator has poles on the light cone $\omega=cq/\sqrt\epsilon$. The longitudinal field is tied to the charge density by Gauss's law at every instant, whatever $c$ is. For the LO phonon of GaAs the light cone sits at $q_c=\sqrt{\epsilon_\infty}\,\omega_{\rm LO}/c\approx6\times10^{-5}$ Å$^{-1}$ (§X.1), about $5\times10^{-5}$ of the zone size. Sending $c\to\infty$ shrinks it to a point and leaves only the longitudinal field.

$\xrightarrow{\;c\to\infty\;}$
$=$
$\xrightarrow{\;\omega\to0\;}$

The section in one line. Rose wavy: full field line, longitudinal plus transverse (heavy: dressed by electrons). Rose dashed: longitudinal (Coulomb) line; double dashed: $W^{\rm e}$. Blue blobs: electronic bubbles $\Pi^{\rm e,0}$. Amber zigzag: phonon; teal dots: ionic current vertices, which in this limit see only $\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma$.

Four sectors, one survivor

In §B.6 the field propagator was assembled from longitudinal and transverse free lines, $D^0=D^{0l}+D^{0t}$ (E.375), and every diagram was sorted into one of four sectors by the type of its two outer lines (EPP Fig. 10, E Eqs. 365–368). The electron-dressed line of §B.7, which contains only electronic bubbles, splits the same way:

$$D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}=D^{{\rm e},ll}_{\mu\nu}+D^{{\rm e},lt}_{\mu\nu}+D^{{\rm e},tl}_{\mu\nu}+D^{{\rm e},tt}_{\mu\nu}\tag{E.433}$$

The transverse free line is

$$D^{0t}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{q^2}\,\frac{q^2\delta_{\mu\nu}-q_\mu q_\nu}{\omega^2-\omega_\bq^2+i\eta},\qquad \omega_\bq=cq\tag{E.372}$$

At fixed $\bq$ and $\omega$ it vanishes like $1/c$. In EPP's words, "in the electrostatic limit ($c\to\infty$) there are no photons" (p. 97). Each term of the $lt$, $tl$ and $tt$ sectors contains at least one $D^{0t}$, hence

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}=D^{{\rm e},ll}_{\mu\nu}\tag{E.434}$$

First-order term of each sector, after EPP Fig. 10 (which draws the full $D$, with ionic bubbles as well). Dashed: longitudinal line $D^{0l}$, the instantaneous Coulomb interaction in vector form; wavy: transverse photon $D^{0t}$; blob: electronic current–current bubble $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj}$. Grey: the three sectors with a transverse outer line, which drop out for $c\to\infty$. The captions give the scaling of the whole sector at fixed $\bq,\omega$. For $tt$ it comes from the zeroth-order term, the free line $D^{0t}$; the first-order term drawn here falls faster, as $c^{-3}$.

One qualification makes the statement precise. $D^{{\rm e},ll}$ itself grows like $c$, because the longitudinal line does:

$$D^{0l}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{q^2}\,\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{\omega^2}\tag{E.374}$$

What enters a physical quantity is $D/c$. Every ionic and electronic current vertex carries a factor $c^{-1/2}$ (E.392, E.414), so the phonon self-energy $\Omega^{\rm e}=-J^*D^{\rm e}J$ is proportional to $D^{\rm e}/c$; EPP's digression E.439 makes the same remark. On that scale the $ll$ sector is of order $c^0$ and the other three vanish like $c^{-2}$. The figure computes this for an anisotropic insulator, where all four sectors are nonzero.

Note on the source: the power counting of E.440

EPP states

$$\begin{aligned}&D^{ll}_{\mu\nu}\sim c,\quad D^{lt}_{\mu\nu}\sim c^0,\\&D^{tl}_{\mu\nu}\sim c^0,\quad\text{and}\quad D^{tt}_{\mu\nu}\sim c^{-1}.\end{aligned}\tag{E.440}$$

The middle two are off by one power. At fixed $\bq,\omega$, $D^{0l}\propto c$ (E.374), $D^{0t}\propto c^{-1}$ (E.372) and $\Pi_{jj}\propto c^{-1}$ (the $1/c$ prefactor of E.383). The lowest $lt$ term, $D^{0l}\Pi D^{0t}$, therefore scales as $c\cdot c^{-1}\cdot c^{-1}=c^{-1}$, and every further pair $\Pi D^{0l}$ adds $c^0$. So $D^{lt}$, $D^{tl}$ and $D^{tt}$ all scale as $c^{-1}$ (derived here, not printed in EPP; steps of this kind are marked [derived] below). The same counting suppresses terms of the $ll$ sector that contain an internal transverse line, such as $D^{0l}\Pi D^{0t}\Pi D^{0l}\propto c^{-1}$, so what survives is the purely longitudinal chain. The conclusion E.434 is unaffected, since it only needs these terms to be subleading.

Derivation: the closed form of $D^{\rm e}$ for a constant dielectric tensor, and its $c\to\infty$ limit

Write the free propagator E.375 in units of $4\pi c/\omega^2$, with $q^2=(\omega/c)^2x^2$:

$$d^0\equiv\frac{\omega^2}{4\pi c}D^0=\frac{\delta-x^2\hat\bq\hat\bq}{x^2-1}=\frac{P_T}{x^2-1}-P_L,\qquad (d^0)^{-1}=(x^2-1)P_T-P_L .$$

With $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj}=\frac{\omega^2}{4\pi c}(\epsilon-1)$, E.388 reads $d^{\rm e}=d^0+d^0(\epsilon-1)d^{\rm e}$, so $(d^{\rm e})^{-1}=(d^0)^{-1}-(\epsilon-1)=x^2P_T-\epsilon$, using $P_L+P_T=1$. The vacuum light line $x=1$ cancels; the poles sit where $\det(x^2P_T-\epsilon)=0$, the light lines of the medium. For $x\to\infty$ only the longitudinal direction escapes the large term $x^2P_T$, and

$$d^{\rm e}\to-\frac{\hat\bq\hat\bq}{\hat\bq\cdot\epsilon\cdot\hat\bq}+O(x^{-2}),$$

which is E.446 with $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}=\epsilon$. The $O(x^{-2})$ remainder contains all of $lt$, $tl$ and $tt$. For an isotropic $\epsilon$, $d^{\rm e}=P_T/(x^2-\epsilon)-P_L/\epsilon$: the two kernels of §B.8.

The survivor is $W^{\rm e}$

The $ll$ sector is Coulomb physics written with vector indices. Undoing the connection formulas of §B.6 (E Eqs. 350, 355, 359–360) turns its scalar core into a familiar Dyson equation, with $v=1/|\br-\br'|$ and $\otimes$ a convolution in space. The index 1 of $D^{\rm e}_{11}$ labels the scalar (Coulomb) row and column of EPP's $4\times4$ propagator, whose free part is $D^0={\rm diag}(v,\hat D^{0t})$ (E.317); it is not the Cartesian $x$.

$$D^{\rm e}_{11}=v+v\otimes\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}\otimes v+\dots=v+v\otimes\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}\otimes D^{\rm e}_{11}\tag{E.435}$$
$$D^{{\rm e},ll}_{\mu\nu}(\br,\br',\omega)=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,\partial_\mu\partial'_\nu D^{\rm e}_{11}(\br,\br',\omega)\tag{E.436}$$

E.435 screens the Coulomb interaction by the electronic density response $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}$ in the RPA, so EPP names it

$$D^{\rm e}_{11}(\br,\br',\omega)\equiv W^{\rm e}(\br,\br',\omega)\tag{E.437}$$

and, for a translationally invariant medium,

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,q_\mu q_\nu\,W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)\tag{E.441}$$

$W^{\rm e}$ itself follows from the dielectric form of the Dyson equation, $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}D^{\rm e}=D^0$ with $\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}=\delta_{\mu\nu}-\sum_\alpha D^0_{\mu\alpha}\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\alpha\nu}$ (E.431–432, §B.8). Inserting E.441 and the $c\to\infty$ limit of $D^0$, then contracting with $\bq$, gives

$$W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)=\frac{4\pi}{\sum_{\mu\nu}q_\mu\,\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)\,q_\nu}\tag{E.445}$$
Derivation: from (E.431) to (E.445), and why this is the RPA dielectric function

For $c\to\infty$ the free propagator E.375 becomes purely longitudinal,

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2}\,\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{q^2}.\tag{E.442}$$

Put E.441 on the left and E.442 on the right of E.431:

$$\sum_\alpha\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\alpha}(\bq,\omega)\,q_\alpha q_\nu\,W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)=4\pi\,\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{q^2}.\tag{E.443}$$

Cancel $q_\nu$ on both sides, multiply by $q_\mu$ and sum:

$$\sum_{\mu\nu}q_\mu\,\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bq,\omega)\,q_\nu\,W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)=4\pi,\tag{E.444}$$

which is E.445. To identify the denominator, insert E.442 into E.432: $\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}\to\delta_{\mu\nu}+\frac{4\pi c}{\omega^2q^2}\,q_\mu\sum_\alpha q_\alpha\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\alpha\nu}$. The longitudinal connection formula $\Pi_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,\bq\cdot\Pi_{jj}\cdot\bq$ (E.350 in $\bq$ space, §B.6) then gives [derived]

$$\frac{\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)\cdot\bq}{q^2}=1-\frac{4\pi}{q^2}\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}(\bq,\omega)\equiv\epsilon^{\rm e}_L(\bq,\omega),\qquad W^{\rm e}=\frac{4\pi}{q^2\,\epsilon^{\rm e}_L(\bq,\omega)} .$$

This is the longitudinal RPA dielectric function, $1-v\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}$, and $W^{\rm e}=v/\epsilon^{\rm e}_L$ is the screened interaction that E.435 sums.

Bridge to Giustino: this is the $W_{\rm e}$ of Hedin–Baym

Giustino's electronic screened interaction (§A.5) is $W_{\rm e}=v+vP_{\rm e}W_{\rm e}$ (G.94), with $\epsilon_{\rm e}=1-vP_{\rm e}$ (G Eq. 95). E.435 is G.94 with $P_{\rm e}\to\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}$, the RPA bubble (Giustino's approximation (i), $\Gamma=\delta\delta$, in G §V.A.3), restricted to $\bG=\bG'=0$. It is the RPA $W$ of a GW code with local fields switched off. EPP reaches it from the other side. Giustino postulates the instantaneous $v$; EPP obtains $W^{\rm e}$ as the part of the full electromagnetic propagator that survives $c\to\infty$. Hedin–Baym's objects are the longitudinal projections of EPP's.

Subtlety: the head of the RPA dielectric matrix

EPP keeps only $\bG=0$ ("CLFs are mostly neglected here", p. 95) and no exchange–correlation. So $\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}\cdot\bq/q^2$ is the head $\epsilon_{00}$ of the RPA dielectric matrix and $W^{\rm e}=v/\epsilon_{00}$, whereas the head of $W$ in a GW code is $v\,\epsilon^{-1}_{00}$ and DFPT's $\epsilon^\infty$ is the macroscopic $1/\epsilon^{-1}_{00}$ with local fields and $f_{xc}$. In sp semiconductors dropping local fields raises $\epsilon^\infty$ by roughly 10% (literature, illustrative). Below, $\epsilon_\infty$ stands for whichever electronic dielectric tensor one trusts.

Phonons dressed by $W^{\rm e}$ give the Gonze–Lee term

Now insert the survivor into the phonon self-energy. In the diagonal approximation of §B.7, with the dynamical ionic vertex $J_{\mu\sigma}\propto\omega j_{\mu\sigma}$ (E.392),

$$\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}(\bq,\omega)=-\frac{\hbar\omega^2}{2c\,\Omega_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma(\bq)}\sum_{\alpha\beta}j^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\,D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\,j_{\beta\sigma}(\bq)\tag{E.450}$$

Here $\omega_\sigma(\bq)$ is the bare phonon frequency, built from short-range force constants only, and $j_{\alpha\sigma}$ the ionic current vertex of mode $\sigma$ (E.295, written out below). With E.441 the prefactor $\omega^2/c$ cancels against $-c/\omega^2$:

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}(\bq,\omega)=\frac{\hbar\,W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)}{2\,\Omega_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma(\bq)}\,\Big|\sum_\alpha q_\alpha\,j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\Big|^2\tag{E.452}$$

A screened Coulomb line is exchanged between two Born-charge dipole currents, and only the component of the mode current along $\bq$ couples: only a longitudinal polarization wave carries bound charge (§A.4). The poles of the phonon propagator (E.405), $\omega^2=\omega_\sigma^2+2\omega_\sigma\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}/\hbar$, become

$$\omega^2=\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+\frac{W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\,\Big|\sum_\alpha q_\alpha\,j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\Big|^2\tag{E.453}$$

This condition is still self-consistent in $\omega$. EPP then argues that "the 3D electronic screening is in the range of phonon energies practically static" (p. 99) and sets $\omega=0$ on the right:

$$\tilde\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)=\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)+\frac{W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega=0)}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\,\Big|\sum_\alpha q_\alpha\,j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)\Big|^2\tag{E.454}$$

For an insulator $W^{\rm e}(\bq,0)=4\pi/(\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\bq)$. Writing out $|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2$ with $j_{\alpha\sigma}=\sum_{a\mu}Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}e_{a\mu\sigma}/\sqrt{m_a}$ (E.295) gives [derived]

$$\tilde\omega^2_\sigma=\omega^2_\sigma+\sum_{a\mu,\,b\nu}\frac{e^*_{a\mu\sigma}}{\sqrt{m_a}}\left[\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\,\frac{(\bq\cdot Z^*_a)_\mu\,(\bq\cdot Z^*_b)_\nu}{\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\bq}\right]\frac{e_{b\nu\sigma}}{\sqrt{m_b}},\qquad (\bq\cdot Z^*_a)_\mu=\sum_\alpha q_\alpha Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}$$

The bracket is the nonanalytic dipole–dipole force constant of Gonze and Lee (cited in Giustino §VI.A.3; see §A.4). In SI and with Giustino's dimensionless Born charges it reads

$$\tilde C^{\rm NA}_{\kappa\alpha,\kappa'\beta}(\bq)=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega}\,\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\,\frac{(\bq\cdot\bZ^*_\kappa)_\alpha\,(\bq\cdot\bZ^*_{\kappa'})_\beta}{\bq\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon^\infty\cdot\bq}$$

and the two agree term by term once $Z^*_{\rm EPP}=|e|Z^*_{\rm G}$ and $e^2\to e^2/4\pi\varepsilon_0$. The agreement holds at small $q$. EPP puts all dipoles of a cell at its origin (E.314), so its $j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bq)$ lacks the basis phases $e^{-i\bq\cdot\boldsymbol\tau_\kappa}$, which are close to 1 only near $\Gamma$. E.454 is first-order perturbation theory in this term on the basis of bare modes, whereas DFPT adds it to the dynamical matrix before diagonalizing. The two coincide whenever the term does not mix modes, as for the optical modes of a cubic diatomic crystal. There $|\bj_\sigma|^2=Z^{*2}/\mu$ ($\mu$ the reduced mass), and for $\bj_\sigma\parallel\hat\bq$

$$\omega_{\rm LO}^2=\omega_{\rm TO}^2+\frac{\omega_p^2}{\epsilon_\infty},\qquad \omega_p^2=\frac{4\pi Z^{*2}}{\Omega_{\rm uc}\,\mu},\qquad \omega_\sigma=\omega_{\rm TO},$$

while modes with $\bj_\sigma\perp\hat\bq$ are not shifted. For GaAs ($Z^*=2.07$, $\Omega_{\rm uc}=45.2$ Å$^3$, $\mu=36.1$ amu, $\epsilon_\infty=10.9$, $\hbar\omega_{\rm TO}=33.3$ meV; literature values, illustrative) this gives $\hbar\omega_p=44.6$ meV and $\hbar\omega_{\rm LO}=35.9$ meV, against 36.2 meV measured. When several polar modes lie close together (perovskites, low-symmetry oxides) the off-diagonal elements $\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}$ of E.399 must be kept, which restores the matrix form. This is the electrostatic splitting, with $c\to\infty$ taken first; the $\bq=0$ result E.410 of §B.7 is the opposite order of limits and describes a different object, the upper polariton without electrons.

Bridge to Giustino: the LO–TO splitting, derived instead of added

In Part A the splitting is put in by hand. DFPT computes analytic force constants and adds the Gonze–Lee term built from $Z^*$ and $\epsilon^\infty$, the same kernel that gives the Verdi–Giustino vertex (G Eq. 180, §A.4; Giustino calls the two strategies analogous in G §VI.A.3). In EPP the term is generated by one $W^{\rm e}$ line between two dipole currents; the Fröhlich vertex is the same line with one dipole replaced by an electronic density (§B.8). The step from E.453 to E.454 is Giustino's adiabatic approximation, "setting $\omega=0$ in Eq. (121)" (G §V.A.1, after Keating 1968), applied to his phonon self-energy (G.121), displayed in §A.5. In G.121 bare nuclear point charges $Z_\kappa$ interact through $W_{\rm e}$. In E.452 Born-charge point dipoles at the cell origins interact through $W^{\rm e}$, and only its long-range part, $\bG=0$, is kept; the short-range part sits in the bare $\omega_\sigma$. So $\Omega^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$ is the dipolar part of Giustino's adiabatic $\Pi^{\rm A}=\Pi^{\rm ph}(\omega=0)$ (G Eq. 125), and $\Omega^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)-\Omega^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$ the dipolar part of his $\Pi^{\rm NA}$.

Note on the source: "probably identical"

EPP calls E.454 "very similar (probably identical)" to Eq. 2 of Sohier, Gibertini, Calandra, Mauri and Marzari, Nano Lett. 17, 3758 (2017), and its 2D counterpart "consistent with" their Eq. 3 (p. 102). The manuscript does not carry out the comparison. What is established is agreement in form: a bare frequency plus a dipole–dipole term screened by the static electronic $W$. That the prefactors and the dielectric object coincide (here the RPA head, there the DFPT dielectric tensor) is not shown. The 2D case is §B.10.

Collecting the limits, Giustino's world is recovered piece by piece:

EPP, finite $c$$c\to\infty$Giustino
$D^{\rm e}$, $3\times3$ (E.388)$-\frac{c}{\omega^2}q_\mu q_\nu W^{\rm e}$ (E.441)$W_{\rm e}=v+vP_{\rm e}W_{\rm e}$ (G Eq. 94), RPA, $\bG=0$
$\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}$ (E.432)$\bq\cdot\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}\cdot\bq/q^2=1-v\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}$$\epsilon_{\rm e}=1-vP_{\rm e}$ (G Eq. 95), head only
$g^{\rm dyn}$ (E.416)Verdi–Giustino with $\epsilon^\infty\to\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$ (§B.8)$g^{\mathcal L}$ (G Eq. 180)

Keeping $\omega$: LO-phonon–plasmon modes

The static step needs the electrons to follow the lattice. In an undoped semiconductor they do: the gap lies far above $\hbar\omega_{\rm LO}$, $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega_{\rm LO})\approx\epsilon_\infty$, and E.454 is the DFPT result. Free carriers change this. Their screened plasma frequency $\omega_{\rm pl}/\sqrt{\epsilon_\infty}$, with $\omega_{\rm pl}^2=4\pi ne^2/m^*$, moves through the phonon range as the density $n$ grows, and near resonance $W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$ is nothing like $W^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$. E.453 must then be solved as it stands.

Take the LO mode of a cubic polar semiconductor, $\bj_\sigma\parallel\hat\bq$, so that $W^{\rm e}|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2/\Omega_{\rm uc}=\omega_p^2/\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$, with $\omega_p$ the ionic plasma frequency defined above. E.453 becomes $\omega^2=\omega_{\rm TO}^2+\omega_p^2/\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$, which is the same as [derived]

$$\epsilon_{\rm tot}(\bq,\omega)\equiv\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)+\frac{\omega_p^2}{\omega_{\rm TO}^2-\omega^2}=0 .$$

The coupled longitudinal modes are the zeros of the total dielectric function, with electrons and ions on the same footing, as §B.6 found from the photon side. For $q\to0$ the carriers respond like a Drude gas, $\epsilon^{\rm e}=\epsilon_\infty-\omega_{\rm pl}^2/\omega^2$, and the zeros are [derived]

$$\omega_\pm^2=\tfrac12\Big[\omega_{\rm LO}^2+\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}^2\pm\sqrt{\big(\omega_{\rm LO}^2+\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}^2\big)^2-4\,\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}^2\,\omega_{\rm TO}^2}\,\Big],\qquad \tilde\omega_{\rm pl}^2=\frac{\omega_{\rm pl}^2}{\epsilon_\infty},$$

where $\omega_{\rm LO}^2=\omega_{\rm TO}^2+\omega_p^2/\epsilon_\infty$ is the undoped LO frequency. At low density $L_+$ is the LO phonon and $L_-$ the plasmon. At high density $L_+$ becomes the plasmon and $L_-\to\omega_{\rm TO}$: the carriers screen the macroscopic field and the LO–TO splitting disappears. In between the branches anticross, where $\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}\approx\omega_{\rm LO}$; for GaAs ($m^*=0.067\,m_e$) that happens at $n\approx7\times10^{17}$ cm$^{-3}$.

The adiabatic version, E.454 with the static RPA screening of the carriers, $\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,0)=\epsilon_\infty+k_{\rm TF}^2/q^2$ for $q\ll2k_F$ (Thomas–Fermi, $k_{\rm TF}^2=6\pi ne^2/E_F$), has a single mode [derived],

$$\tilde\omega^2=\omega_{\rm TO}^2+\omega_p^2\,\frac{q^2}{\epsilon_\infty q^2+k_{\rm TF}^2},$$

which slides down to $\omega_{\rm TO}$ as soon as $q$ drops below the screened Thomas–Fermi wavevector $k_{\rm TF}/\sqrt{\epsilon_\infty}$, at any density, and misses the second branch altogether.

Derivation: coupled-mode condition, closed form and spectral functions

For the diatomic LO mode, $|\bq\cdot\bj_\sigma|^2=q^2Z^{*2}/\mu$ and $W^{\rm e}=4\pi/(q^2\epsilon^{\rm e})$, so the shift in E.453 is $\omega_p^2/\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$. Multiplying $\omega^2-\omega_{\rm TO}^2=\omega_p^2/\epsilon^{\rm e}$ by $\epsilon^{\rm e}/(\omega_{\rm TO}^2-\omega^2)$ gives $\epsilon^{\rm e}+\omega_p^2/(\omega_{\rm TO}^2-\omega^2)=0$. With $\epsilon^{\rm e}=\epsilon_\infty-\omega_{\rm pl}^2/\omega^2$ and a factor $\omega^2(\omega_{\rm TO}^2-\omega^2)/\epsilon_\infty$ this is the quadratic in $\omega^2$

$$\omega^4-\omega^2\big(\omega_{\rm LO}^2+\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}^2\big)+\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}^2\,\omega_{\rm TO}^2=0,$$

whose roots are $\omega_\pm^2$. The product of the roots shows that $L_-\to\omega_{\rm TO}$ when $\tilde\omega_{\rm pl}\to\infty$. Static screening instead puts $\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$ into E.454, which yields the single Thomas–Fermi mode. With causal damping ($i\eta\to i\gamma_{\rm ph}\omega$, as in EPP's digression on p. 88) the phonon propagator E.405 is $\hbar F_\sigma=2\omega_{\rm TO}/[\omega^2-\omega_{\rm TO}^2-\omega_p^2/\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)+i\gamma_{\rm ph}\omega]$. Dividing by $\hbar$ gives an inverse energy, $F_\sigma=2\hbar\omega_{\rm TO}/[(\hbar\omega)^2-(\hbar\omega_{\rm TO})^2-(\hbar\omega_p)^2/\epsilon^{\rm e}+i\hbar\gamma_{\rm ph}\,\hbar\omega]$, which panel (b) plots in meV$^{-1}$. Its poles are the zeros of $\epsilon_{\rm tot}$, which are also the peaks of $-{\rm Im}\,1/\epsilon_{\rm tot}$. The two spectral functions share their poles and differ in the weights: the loss function weights the field, $F_\sigma$ the lattice.

When is the static step safe? The electrons must respond faster than the lattice: either collectively, with the plasmon (or, in an insulator, the interband gap) far above $\omega_{\rm LO}$, or one by one, with $qv_F\gg\omega_{\rm LO}$, so that carriers cross a wavelength within a phonon period. EPP's "practically static" argument holds for undoped 3D semiconductors. It fails near the anticrossing. At small $q$ it also fails for dilute carriers whose plasmon lies below the phonon: then $W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega_{\rm LO})$ is close to the undoped $4\pi/q^2\epsilon_\infty$, while $W^{\rm e}(\bq,0)$ is fully screened.

Bridge to Giustino: the speculation of §V.A.2, realized

Giustino expects new structure in the phonon spectrum "whenever $\epsilon_{\rm e}(\br,\br',\omega)$ exhibits dynamical structure close to vibrational frequencies", for instance in degenerate polar semiconductors, where phonons and plasmons combine into coupled plasmon–phonon modes, "the electronic analog of photon polaritons", predicted by Varga (1965) and confirmed by Raman measurements on GaAs (Mooradian and Wright 1966). He speculates that they should follow from the frequency dependence of the phonon self-energy in his Eq. (136) (G §V.A.2, p. 015003-23; see §A.6). E.453 does exactly this. In his language the plasmon pole lives entirely in $\Pi^{\rm NA}$, which is why no adiabatic, DFPT-type calculation can produce the $L_\pm$ pair. EPP holds both analogues side by side: phonon polaritons from transverse photons (§B.7), and plasmon–phonon modes from the longitudinal $W^{\rm e}(\omega)$.

Subtlety: two corners of the Lindhard function

The Drude form ($\omega\gg qv_F$) and the Thomas–Fermi form ($\omega\ll qv_F$) are opposite corners of one function, and their $\omega,\bq\to0$ limits do not commute (Giustino recalls that the electron-gas dielectric function diverges as $\omega,\bq\to0$, G §V.A.1). The heat map uses the full Lindhard function. It ignores nonparabolicity, local fields and finite temperature. In GaAs the $T=0$ picture is a stretch at room temperature below about $3\times10^{17}$ cm$^{-3}$, where $E_F$ drops below $k_BT$ and the carriers become nondegenerate [derived].

In short: with $c\to\infty$ and $\omega\to0$, EPP returns the world of DFPT, with the electronic $W$ of Hedin–Baym, the Gonze–Lee LO–TO term and the Verdi–Giustino vertex, now produced by one propagator instead of being added by hand. Relax either limit and something new appears. Finite $c$ gives phonon polaritons (§B.7) and photon-mediated TO coupling (§B.8); finite $\omega$ gives the plasmon–phonon modes above. In a 2D crystal the same $W^{\rm e}$ becomes the Rytova–Keldysh interaction and removes the splitting at $\Gamma$ (§B.10).

B.10EPP §8 · Eqs. 455–472

Two-dimensional crystals: no LO–TO splitting at Γ

A polar monolayer talks to the electromagnetic field only at $z=0$. By the end you can derive EPP's 2D phonon self-energy, reduce it to the strictly two-dimensional screened interaction $W^{\rm e,2D}=v_Q/\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}$, and explain why the LO branch then starts at the TO frequency and rises linearly, with the same screening length $r_0$ that sets Rytova–Keldysh exciton binding in 2D BSE.

Section B.9 derived the bulk electrostatic result, E Eq. 454. With static electronic screening, $W^{\rm e}(\bq,0)=4\pi/(\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\bq)$, the factor $q^2$ in $|\bq\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma|^2$ cancels against the Coulomb kernel:

$$\tilde\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)-\omega^2_\sigma(\bq)=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\,\frac{|\hat\bq\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma(\bq)|^2}{\hat\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\hat\bq}\qquad(\text{3D, cf. E.454})$$

The shift depends on the direction of $\bq$ but not on its length, so it survives at $\Gamma$. That is the LO–TO splitting. EPP §8 repeats the construction for a single polar layer. Units stay Gaussian, so a sheet has the Coulomb kernel $v_Q=2\pi/Q$. Born charges carry the dimension of charge, $\bQ=(Q_x,Q_y)$ is an in-plane wave vector, and all symbols are EPP's own: nothing is renamed in this section.

Physical picture: where does the depolarization field go?

An LO phonon is a polarization wave, $P\propto\cos Qx$, along its own wave vector. Its bound charge $-\partial_xP$ piles up where the dipoles converge. In bulk these charges form infinite planes, and the field between charged planes does not depend on their spacing: it is the capacitor field $-4\pi P/\epsilon_\infty$ at every wavelength, which stiffens the LO mode equally for every $q$. In a monolayer the bound charge sits on a line inside the sheet. Its field lines bulge out into the vacuum or the substrate, to a distance of about $1/Q$, before closing on the opposite charge. The longer the wavelength, the weaker the in-plane field. At $Q\to0$ only the short-range springs remain, so LO and TO are degenerate.

A sheet of point dipoles

EPP builds the ionic photon self-energy from Born-charge point dipoles on the lattice sites (§B.5). For a monolayer all sites lie in the plane $z=0$. Repeating the lattice sums with 2D wave vectors (EPP pp. 64 and 66–67) gives paramagnetic and diamagnetic parts confined to the sheet:

$$\Pi^{\rm ion,para}_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')=-\frac{\hbar}{cS_{\rm uc}}\sum_{\sigma=1}^{3s}\frac{\omega_\sigma(\bQ)}{2}\,j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bQ)\,j^*_{\beta\sigma}(\bQ)\,F_\sigma(\bQ,\omega)\,\delta(z)\delta(z')\tag{E.300}$$
$$\Pi^{\rm ion,dia}_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')=-\frac{1}{S_{\rm uc}c}\sum_{a\mu}\frac{1}{m_a}\,Z^*_{a\alpha\mu}Z^*_{a\beta\mu}\,\delta(z)\delta(z')\tag{E.305}$$

The diamagnetic term cancels the static paramagnetic one exactly as in 3D, by completeness of the phonon eigenvectors (E Eqs. 306–310). The strictly 2D electronic bubble of a layer (E Eq. 285) has the same sheet form. The ionic self-energy of the sheet is therefore the bulk one, renormalized from volume to area:

$$\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')=\frac{\Omega_{\rm uc}}{S_{\rm uc}}\,\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}(\bQ,\omega)\,\delta(z)\delta(z')\tag{E.455}$$

Here $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}(\bQ,\omega)$ is the bare ionic bubble of E Eq. 391, which carries $1/\Omega_{\rm uc}$; the prefactor replaces it by $1/S_{\rm uc}$. The δ functions pin both ends of every ionic bubble to $z=0$. The resummation of §B.7 therefore goes through with two replacements (E Eqs. 456–457): $D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bq,\omega)\to D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0)$ and $\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}(\bq,\omega)\to(\Omega_{\rm uc}/S_{\rm uc})\,\Pi^{\rm ion}_{jj}(\bQ,\omega)$. The phonon self-energy of a 2D crystal is

$$\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma'}(\bQ,\omega)=-\sum_{\alpha\beta}J^*_{\alpha\sigma}(\bQ,\omega)\,D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0)\,J_{\beta\sigma'}(\bQ,\omega),\tag{E.458}$$
$$J_{\mu\sigma}(\bQ,\omega)=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2cS_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma(\bQ)}}\;\omega\,j_{\mu\sigma}(\bQ).\tag{E.459}$$

The real change is in the photon line. It is evaluated in the plane of the sheet and obeys a $z$-resolved Dyson equation (unnumbered, EPP p. 100), in which the electronic bubble may spread over the thickness of the layer:

$$\begin{aligned}D^{\rm e}_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')&=D^0_{\alpha\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')\\&\quad+\sum_{\mu\nu}\int_{-l/2}^{l/2}dz_1dz_2\,D^0_{\alpha\mu}(\bQ,\omega,z,z_1)\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{jj\mu\nu}(\bQ,\omega,z_1,z_2)\,D^{\rm e}_{\nu\beta}(\bQ,\omega,z_2,z')\end{aligned}$$

This is where crystal local-field effects along $z$ enter, the same effects that a supercell RPA calculation of a monolayer has to handle.

Subtlety: “Ω → S” is not enough, and out-of-plane dipoles are dropped

EPP p. 86 calls the transition to 2D trivial: $\Omega\to S$, $\Omega_{\rm uc}\to S_{\rm uc}$, $\bq\to\bQ$. That holds for the self-energies, which carry $\delta(z)\delta(z')$, but not for the photon line. A sheet exchanges photons with itself only at $z=z'=0$, so it sees the vacuum propagator of E Eq. 375 integrated over $q_z$ (derived, not printed in EPP), for in-plane $\mu,\nu$:

$$D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bQ,\omega;0,0)=\int\frac{dq_z}{2\pi}\,D^0_{\mu\nu}(\bQ,q_z,\omega)=\frac{2\pi c}{\omega^2\beta}\left(\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}\delta_{\mu\nu}-Q_\mu Q_\nu\right),\qquad\beta=\sqrt{Q^2-\frac{\omega^2}{c^2}}$$

Its longitudinal projection is $-2\pi c\beta/\omega^2$, which tends to $-\frac{c}{\omega^2}Q^2v_Q$ for $c\to\infty$. The kernel $v_Q=2\pi/Q$ thus comes from the $q_z$ integral, not from a change of normalization. The $zz$ component contains a contact term $\propto\delta(z-z')$, the depolarization field of a sheet of out-of-plane dipoles. EPP discards it as the “divergent local term” before E Eq. 463 and keeps only $\alpha=x,y$ from there on, although E Eq. 300 contains out-of-plane dipoles. Everything below applies to in-plane modes (the in-plane LO/TO pair of hBN or the E′ mode of MoS₂), and everything except the last subsection and its figure tab is electrostatic. ZO-type modes with $Z^*_{zz}$ receive a $Q$-independent depolarization shift instead.

The electrostatic limit: a strictly 2D screened interaction

For $c\to\infty$ only the longitudinal sector survives, as in bulk. The partial Fourier transform of E Eq. 438 gives

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')\equiv-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\left[i\bQ+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right]\left[-i\bQ+\frac{\partial}{\partial z'}\right]W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,z,z').\tag{E.460}$$

The brackets are the 3-vectors $(iQ_x,iQ_y,\partial_z)$ and $(-iQ_x,-iQ_y,\partial_{z'})$, of which components $\mu$ and $\nu$ are taken. EPP then switches off the electronic local fields along $z$ and squeezes the electronic bubble into the sheet, $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')\approx\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}(\bQ,\omega)\delta(z)\delta(z')$, with the 2D RPA polarizability (unnumbered, EPP p. 101; SBZ is the surface Brillouin zone):

$$\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}(\bQ,\omega)=\frac{2}{S}\sum_{\mathbf K\in{\rm SBZ}}\sum_{nm}\frac{f_{n\mathbf K}-f_{m\mathbf K+\bQ}}{\hbar\omega+E_{n\mathbf K}-E_{m\mathbf K+\bQ}+i\eta}\,\left|\rho_{n\mathbf K,m\mathbf K+\bQ}\right|^2$$

Summing the RPA chain of sheet bubbles gives the screened Coulomb interaction between heights $z$ and $z'$:

$$W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,z,z')=v_Q\,e^{-Q|z-z'|}+v_Q^2\,e^{-Q(|z|+|z'|)}\,\Pi^{\rm e}_{\rho\rho}(\bQ,\omega),\tag{E.461}$$
$$\Pi^{\rm e}_{\rho\rho}=\frac{\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}}{1-v_Q\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}},\tag{E.462}$$

with $v_Q=2\pi/Q$. The first term is the bare Coulomb interaction after the in-plane Fourier transform. The second is the potential of the charge induced in the sheet, which decays away from it as $e^{-Q|z|}$. For in-plane components no $z$-derivatives appear in E Eq. 460, and at $z=z'=0$ (E Eq. 463)

$$\lim_{c\to\infty}D^{\rm e}_{\mu\nu}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0)\equiv-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,Q_\mu Q_\nu\,W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0);\qquad\mu,\nu=x,y.\tag{E.464}$$

Inserted into E Eq. 458 with the vertices of E Eq. 459 (this is E Eq. 465), it gives

$$\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}(\bQ,\omega)=\frac{\hbar\,W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0)}{2S_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma(\bQ)}\left|\sum_{\alpha=x,y}j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bQ)\,Q_\alpha\right|^2.\tag{E.466}$$

The 2D phonon propagator keeps the bulk form of E Eq. 405 (E Eq. 467), so the renormalized frequencies solve

$$\omega^2=\omega^2_\sigma(\bQ)+\frac{W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0)}{S_{\rm uc}}\left|\sum_{\alpha=x,y}j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bQ)\,Q_\alpha\right|^2.\tag{E.468}$$

In the plane, E Eqs. 461–462 collapse to the form every 2D RPA practitioner knows:

$$W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,z=0,z'=0)\equiv W^{\rm e,2D}(\bQ,\omega)=\frac{v_Q}{\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,\omega)},\tag{E.469}$$
$$\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,\omega)=1-v_Q\,\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}(\bQ,\omega).\tag{E.470}$$

With a static electronic response, $\omega=0$ inside $W$ (E Eq. 471), EPP's final result is

$$\tilde\omega^2_\sigma(\bQ)=\omega^2_\sigma(\bQ)+\frac{1}{S_{\rm uc}}\,\frac{v_Q}{\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,\omega=0)}\left|\sum_{\alpha=x,y}j_{\alpha\sigma}(\bQ)\,Q_\alpha\right|^2.\tag{E.472}$$
Derivation: from E.461 to E.469, and from E.465 to E.468

The in-plane screened interaction. At $z=z'=0$ both exponentials in E Eq. 461 equal 1. With E Eq. 462,

$$W^{\rm e}(\bQ,\omega,0,0)=v_Q+v_Q^2\,\frac{\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}}{1-v_Q\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}}=v_Q\,\frac{1-v_Q\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}+v_Q\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}}{1-v_Q\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}}=\frac{v_Q}{1-v_Q\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}},$$

which is E Eqs. 469–470. E Eq. 461 is the solution of $W=v+v\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}W$ when the bubble is a δ function in $z$ and $v(\bQ,z,z')=v_Qe^{-Q|z-z'|}$ is the in-plane transform of $1/|\br-\br'|$.

The self-energy. E Eq. 465 is E Eq. 458 for $\sigma=\sigma'$ with E Eq. 459 inserted: $J^*_{\alpha\sigma}J_{\beta\sigma}=\frac{\hbar\omega^2}{2cS_{\rm uc}\omega_\sigma}j^*_{\alpha\sigma}j_{\beta\sigma}$. Now insert E Eq. 464:

$$\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}=-\frac{\hbar\omega^2}{2cS_{\rm uc}\omega_\sigma}\sum_{\alpha\beta=x,y}j^*_{\alpha\sigma}\left(-\frac{c}{\omega^2}Q_\alpha Q_\beta W^{\rm e}\right)j_{\beta\sigma}=\frac{\hbar W^{\rm e}}{2S_{\rm uc}\omega_\sigma}\Big|\sum_{\alpha}j_{\alpha\sigma}Q_\alpha\Big|^2 .$$

The factors $\omega^2$ and $c$ cancel, as in bulk (E Eq. 452). The poles of E Eq. 467 satisfy $\omega^2=\omega_\sigma^2+2\omega_\sigma\Omega^{\rm e}_{\sigma\sigma}/\hbar$, which gives E Eq. 468.

The 3D check. The same steps with $\Omega_{\rm uc}$, $v(q)=4\pi/q^2$ and $\epsilon_\infty$ give the bulk shift at the top of this section. Only the Coulomb kernel and the cell measure differ.

Why LO meets TO at Γ

Put the two results side by side, for a mode with in-plane dipole $\mathbf j_\sigma$:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{3D:}\quad&\tilde\omega^2_\sigma-\omega^2_\sigma=\frac{4\pi}{\Omega_{\rm uc}}\,\frac{q^2\,|\hat\bq\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma|^2}{q^2\;\hat\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\hat\bq}\;\xrightarrow{\;q\to0\;}\;\text{const},\\[4pt]\text{2D:}\quad&\tilde\omega^2_\sigma-\omega^2_\sigma=\frac{2\pi}{S_{\rm uc}}\,\frac{Q^2\,|\hat\bQ\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma|^2}{Q\;\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,0)}\;\xrightarrow{\;Q\to0\;}\;0.\end{aligned}$$

The vertex $|\bQ\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma|^2$ supplies $Q^2$ in both cases. The 3D kernel removes $q^2$; the sheet kernel removes only one power of $Q$. For an insulator $\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,0)$ tends to a finite value as $Q\to0$, so the LO branch leaves the TO frequency with a finite slope (derived from E Eq. 472):

$$\hbar\,\frac{d\tilde\omega_{\rm LO}}{dQ}\bigg|_{Q=0}=\frac{\pi\hbar\,|\hat\bQ\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma|^2}{S_{\rm uc}\,\omega_\sigma\,\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(0,0)}$$

TO modes, with $\hat\bQ\cdot\mathbf j_\sigma=0$, are not shifted in either case. The first figure shows the same counting in real space: without electronic screening the 2D shift is the 3D one times $Qd/2$, for a layer of thickness $d$ with $\Omega_{\rm uc}=S_{\rm uc}d$.

Agreement with Sohier et al. 2017 is in form

EPP's comparisons with Sohier et al., Nano Lett. 17, 3758 (2017) (E Eq. 454 "probably identical" to their Eq. 2, E Eq. 472 "consistent with" their Eq. 3) are agreements in form, not term-by-term identities; see the note in §B.9. Two points from the literature, not from EPP: Sohier et al. take their screening from DFPT, which includes local fields and exchange–correlation, rather than the strictly 2D RPA of E Eq. 470; and in a 3D-periodic supercell the periodic images restore a spurious splitting unless the Coulomb interaction is truncated in $z$.

Bridge to Giustino

Giustino's treatment of polar coupling is three-dimensional. The LO–TO splitting it points to (the Gonze–Lee nonanalytic term, cited in Giustino §VI.A.3 but not printed) carries $\epsilon^\infty$, and its long-range vertex is the Verdi–Giustino form $\propto(\bq\cdot\mathbf Z^*_\kappa\cdot\mathbf e_{\kappa\nu})/(\bq\cdot\epsilon^\infty\cdot\bq)$ (Giustino §VI.A.3, Eq. G.180; §A.4). Both rest on the 3D kernel $4\pi/q^2$. EPP's 2D result follows from the single replacement $4\pi/(\bq\cdot\epsilon_\infty\cdot\bq)\to2\pi/[Q\,\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,0)]$. Applied to the electrostatic vertex of §B.8, the same replacement turns the $1/q$ Fröhlich divergence into a coupling that tends to a finite value, $\propto\hat\bQ\cdot Z^*\cdot\mathbf e/\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}(\bQ,0)$, as $Q\to0$ (derived, not in EPP). In Giustino's language (his phonon self-energy is written $\Pi^{\rm ph}$ on this page), E Eq. 472 is the long-range part of the adiabatic phonon self-energy $\Pi^{\rm A}=\Pi^{\rm ph}(\omega=0)$ (Eq. G.125, §A.6), the part DFPT adds through $Z^*$ and $\epsilon^\infty$, now evaluated with a two-dimensional $W_{\rm e}$.

The same $r_0$ that sets your exciton binding

For a gapped layer the static sheet bubble is quadratic at small $Q$, $\Pi^{\rm e,0}_{\rho\rho}(\bQ,0)\approx-\alpha_{\rm 2D}Q^2$, where $\alpha_{\rm 2D}$ is the in-plane sheet polarizability (a length in Gaussian units). E Eq. 470 then gives $\epsilon^{\rm e}_{\rm 2D}=1+r_0Q$ with $r_0=2\pi\alpha_{\rm 2D}$, and $W^{\rm e,2D}=2\pi/[Q(1+r_0Q)]$ is the Rytova–Keldysh interaction of 2D BSE and Wannier-exciton models. A substrate below and a capping layer above, with dielectric constants $\epsilon_{\rm a}$ and $\epsilon_{\rm b}$, add the environment. This is standard electrostatics and a literature parameterization; EPP itself treats a freestanding sheet:

$$\epsilon_{\rm 2D}(Q)=\epsilon_{\rm env}+r_0Q,\qquad\epsilon_{\rm env}=\tfrac12(\epsilon_{\rm a}+\epsilon_{\rm b})$$

Some papers write $\epsilon_{\rm env}(1+r_0'Q)$ with $r_0'=r_0/\epsilon_{\rm env}$. For a diatomic in-plane mode $|\hat\bQ\cdot\mathbf j_{\rm LO}|^2=Z^{*2}/\mu$, and E Eq. 472 becomes

$$\begin{aligned}(\hbar\tilde\omega_{\rm LO})^2&=(\hbar\omega_{\rm T})^2+\frac{C\,Q}{\epsilon_{\rm env}+r_0Q},\\ C&=\frac{2\pi e^2Z^{*2}\hbar^2}{S_{\rm uc}\,\mu}=0.3782\,\frac{Z^{*2}}{S_{\rm uc}[\text{Å}^2]\;\mu[\text{u}]}\ \text{eV}^2\,\text{Å},\end{aligned}$$

with $Z^*$ in units of $|e|$ and $e^2=14.40$ eV Å. Two regimes meet at $Q^*=\epsilon_{\rm env}/r_0$:

  • $Q\ll Q^*$: a linear rise with slope $C/(2\hbar\omega_{\rm T}\epsilon_{\rm env})$. Encapsulation divides the slope by $\epsilon_{\rm env}$.
  • $Q\gg Q^*$: the sheet's own electrons dominate the screening, and $(\hbar\tilde\omega_{\rm LO})^2\to(\hbar\omega_{\rm T})^2+C/r_0$. This plateau does not depend on the environment.

These are the two regimes of the Keldysh potential in real space: $1/(\epsilon_{\rm env}r)$ for $r\gg r_0/\epsilon_{\rm env}$, logarithmic inside. An exciton of radius $a_X$ samples $W$ around $Q\sim1/a_X$; an LO phonon of wave vector $Q$ samples the same function at the same $Q$. If your BSE workflow already gives you $r_0$, the LO dispersion needs only $Z^*$ and the mode eigenvector on top. With hBN numbers ($S_{\rm uc}=5.43$ Å², $Z^*=2.7$, $\mu=6.10$ u, $\hbar\omega_{\rm T}=170$ meV, $r_0=10$ Å; literature values, illustrative) one finds $C=0.0832$ eV² Å, an initial slope of 0.245 eV Å, $\hbar\tilde\omega_{\rm LO}=181.8$ meV at $Q=0.1$ Å$^{-1}$, and a plateau at 193 meV, close to the bulk LO near 200 meV.

Why the plateau looks like bulk, and where the model stops

A layer of thickness $d$ cut from a bulk crystal has $r_0\approx d(\epsilon_\infty-1)/2$ (a common literature estimate). Then $C/r_0=4\pi|\mathbf j|^2/[\Omega_{\rm uc}(\epsilon_\infty-1)]$ with $\Omega_{\rm uc}=S_{\rm uc}d$: the plateau is the bulk splitting of E Eq. 454 with $\epsilon_\infty-1$ in place of $\epsilon_\infty$ (derived). It is also where the strictly 2D model is least trustworthy, because $Qd$ approaches 1 and the finite thickness neglected in E Eq. 461 starts to matter. EPP's $W$ is RPA without local fields or exchange–correlation; a production calculation would use the macroscopic, $z$-truncated $\epsilon$ of the layer.

Doped sheets: plasmon–phonon modes in one sample

E Eq. 471 sets $\omega=0$ inside $W$. As in bulk (§B.9), that fails when free carriers put a plasmon near the phonon. Keep the dynamical $W$ of E Eq. 468 and describe the carriers by a Drude sheet, $\epsilon_{\rm 2D}(Q,\omega)=\epsilon_{\rm env}+r_0Q-\omega_{\rm pl}^2(Q)/\omega^2$ with $\omega_{\rm pl}^2=2\pi ne^2Q/m^*$ (Gaussian, $n$ per area). E Eq. 468 becomes a quadratic in $\omega^2$ (derived):

$$(\epsilon_{\rm env}+r_0Q)\,\omega^4-\omega^2\Big[(\epsilon_{\rm env}+r_0Q)\,\omega_{\rm T}^2+\omega_{\rm pl}^2+C'Q\Big]+\omega_{\rm pl}^2\,\omega_{\rm T}^2=0,\qquad C'=C/\hbar^2$$

The 2D plasmon rises as $\sqrt Q$ from zero, so a single doped sample shows the whole anticrossing as a function of $Q$, where bulk GaAs needs a series of densities. At small $Q$ the upper branch is LO-like and starts at $\omega_{\rm T}$. Beyond the crossing it turns plasmon-like, and the lower branch is pushed below $\omega_{\rm T}$: below the plasmon frequency the carriers overscreen, $\epsilon_{\rm 2D}\lt0$, which reverses the sign of the shift. Even the weakly polar MoS₂-like sheet, whose undoped LO shift is a fraction of a meV, shows an anticrossing of about 4 meV: at resonance the splitting grows as the square root of the coupling, $\sqrt{C'Q/\epsilon_{\rm 2D}}$, not linearly. The Drude form is the local limit of the 2D Lindhard function. It holds while the plasmon lies well above the intraband electron–hole continuum, $\omega\gg v_FQ$, and it drops both the $(v_FQ/\omega)^2$ correction to the plasmon dispersion and Landau damping. At the crossing of both presets $\hbar v_FQ\lesssim0.4\,\hbar\omega_{\rm T}$ (our estimate), so the curves are qualitatively right there.

Finite $c$: when the sheet radiates

Keeping $c$ finite (retardation in EPP's sense) means keeping $\beta$ in the sheet propagator. For a sheet inside a homogeneous medium $\epsilon_{\rm env}$, the longitudinal pole condition gives (derived with the same $q_z$ integral, now in the medium; not in EPP)

$$\omega^2=\omega_{\rm T}^2+\frac{C'\beta}{\epsilon_{\rm env}+r_0\beta},\qquad\beta=\sqrt{Q^2-\epsilon_{\rm env}\,\omega^2/c^2}.$$

Outside the light cone $\beta\lt Q$, and the shift falls to zero at the light line. Inside it $\beta$ is imaginary and the in-plane polar modes radiate. At $Q=0$ the radiative width (FWHM) is $\hbar\gamma_0=C/(\hbar c\sqrt{\epsilon_{\rm env}})$, about 42 μeV for freestanding hBN. It varies as $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ for the p-polarized, LO-like mode and as $1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$ for the s-polarized, TO-like mode, with $x=cQ/(\sqrt{\epsilon_{\rm env}}\,\omega_{\rm T})$. The same two laws govern the radiative widths of in-plane 2D excitons (literature, quantum-well excitons). All of it happens at $Q\lesssim10^{-4}$ Å$^{-1}$, where the electrostatic shift is itself only tens of μeV. The smallness of this window is why E Eq. 472 is safe for phonon physics.

Note on the source

E Eq. 455 is introduced as “your $\Pi^{\rm ion,0}_{jj}$” but written without the superscript 0; both it and E Eq. 391, to which it refers, are the bare ionic bubble (notation switch of EPP p. 87). The “divergent local term” dropped before E Eq. 463 exists only in the $zz$ component (see the subtlety box above). The thickness $l$ in the $z$-resolved Dyson equation and “SBZ” are not defined (read: layer thickness, surface Brillouin zone). Typo: “the the 2D dielectric function” (p. 102).

This is where the EPP manuscript ends. Section Z.1 collects what EPP adds to Giustino's picture and lists what is still open, including the out-of-plane modes and the full finite-$c$ sheet problem set aside here.

Z.1Summary · open questions

What EPP adds, and what is still open

The two formalisms side by side in eight statements, a table of where the electromagnetic extension changes the numbers, and the pieces the EPP manuscript has not yet worked out.

Eight statements to take away

  1. Same lattice, same normal modes. Both start from harmonic force constants, the dynamical matrix and phonon ladder operators (§A.1, §B.1). The difference is which force constants are allowed. EPP must use only the short-range (analytic) part, because it regenerates the long-range dipole–dipole part itself.
  2. Giustino folds the Coulomb physics into numbers. EPP keeps it as a field. In Part A, $\varepsilon_{n\bk}$, $\omega_{\bq\nu}$ and the screened vertex $g_{mn\nu}(\bk,\bq)$ already contain all Coulomb effects (§A.2, §A.3). In Part B the Lagrangian has no electron–phonon term at all. Electrons and ions talk only through the vector potential (§B.2).
  3. Coulomb is the longitudinal photon. In the temporal gauge, the energy of the longitudinal field becomes, via Gauss's law, the full instantaneous Coulomb interaction of electrons and ionic bound charges (§B.4). Charge conservation then rewrites every density vertex as a current vertex. It also turns $v$ into $D^{0l}$, so the free propagator is the vacuum Maxwell propagator $D^0=D^{0l}+D^{0t}$ (§B.6).
  4. One self-energy for all matter. Giustino's polarization $P=\delta\langle\hat n\rangle/\delta V_{\rm tot}$ (G.89), the response of the total electron-plus-nuclear charge, becomes EPP's current–current self-energy $\Pi_{jj}=\Pi^{\rm e}+\Pi^{\rm ion}$. It is gauge invariant only when the diamagnetic terms are kept, $\Pi=\Pi^{\rm para}(\omega)-\Pi^{\rm para}(0)$ (§B.5). The ionic part is exact in the harmonic approximation.
  5. $W$ is a projection of $D$. Giustino's $W=W_{\rm e}+W_{\rm e}\mathcal D W_{\rm e}$ (§A.5) is the longitudinal–longitudinal sector of EPP's $D=D^0+D^0\Pi_{jj}D$, and $W^{\rm e}=D^{\rm e}_{11}$ (§B.9).
  6. The order of limits matters. At $q=0$ with finite $c$, the mode that shifts is the upper phonon polariton, with an unscreened oscillator strength (E.410). The familiar electrostatic LO–TO splitting appears only when $c\to\infty$ is taken first (E.454), and it then coincides with the Gonze–Lee nonanalytic term (§B.7, §B.9).
  7. The Fröhlich vertex becomes dynamical. Photon exchange between an electronic and an ionic current gives a frequency-dependent vertex. For $c\to\infty$ it reduces to the Verdi–Giustino vertex with $\epsilon^\infty\to\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$. The phonon self-energy keeps Giustino's structure of one bare and one screened vertex (§B.8, §A.6).
  8. In 2D there is no LO–TO splitting at Γ. With the strictly two-dimensional $W^{\rm e,2D}=v_Q/\epsilon^{\rm e}_{2D}$ the LO shift grows linearly from zero. The screening length $r_0$ that sets its saturation is the same one that controls Rytova–Keldysh exciton screening (§B.10).

For RPA, GW and BSE practitioners

Most objects in Part B are already familiar from these methods, written in vector form. The electronic photon self-energy $\Pi^{\rm e}$ is the Adler–Wiser response with current vertices. Its longitudinal projection, $\Pi_{\rho\rho}=-\frac{c}{\omega^2}\,\bq\cdot\Pi_{jj}\cdot\bq$, is the familiar density response $\chi^0$. The screened interaction $W^{\rm e}$ that dresses the phonons in §B.9 and §B.10 is the RPA $W$ without local fields. What is new is the transverse sector. It matters only inside the light cone, $q\lesssim q_c=\sqrt{\epsilon_\infty}\,\omega/c$, which is $10^{-5}$–$10^{-4}$ Å$^{-1}$ for vibrational frequencies and about $10^{-3}$ Å$^{-1}$ for a 2 eV exciton (§X.1).

Where the electromagnetic extension changes the numbers

The two kinds of retardation of §X.1 sort the observables. A finite speed of light acts only inside the light cone just quoted. Frequency-dependent electronic screening acts at any $q$ wherever $\hat\epsilon^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$ has structure near the phonon frequencies; Giustino's theory contains it, and EPP keeps it in the vertex instead of setting $g(\omega)\simeq g(0)$ (§B.8). Outside these two windows Part A already gives the answer.

Doped polar semiconductorsPlasmon–phonon modes expected from the nonadiabatic $\Pi^{\rm NA}$ (G §V.A.2) but not evaluated.Coupled LO-phonon–plasmon modes $L_\pm$ from the dynamical $W^{\rm e}(\bq,\omega)$ in E.453, already at $c\to\infty$.A.6, B.9
Polar 2D crystalsNot treated.No LO–TO splitting at Γ, and an LO dispersion set by the same $r_0$ as Rytova–Keldysh screening. Inside the cone the modes radiate, with widths of order 40 μeV for freestanding hBN (worked out on this page, not in the manuscript).B.10
Excitons, exciton–phonon couplingOnly cited (BSE combined with Allen–Heine theory, G p. 42); (G.200) is independent-particle.Outside EPP too: $\Pi^{\rm e}$ is the RPA bubble, with no electron–hole ladder (list below).B.5

What the manuscript does not yet contain

  • Short-range coupling. The EPP Lagrangian freezes the crystal potential at equilibrium, so deformation-potential coupling (acoustic phonons, non-polar optical phonons) is absent. Only the polar, long-range channel is extended.
  • Electron self-energies. EPP dresses photons and phonons but derives no electron self-energy from combined photon and phonon exchange. Giustino's Fan–Migdal and Debye–Waller terms (§A.7) have no EPP counterpart yet. Neither do the temperature-dependent gaps and lifetimes built on them (§A.8).
  • Exchange–correlation, local fields and excitons. The electronic response is RPA without crystal local-field effects (no $\bG,\bG'$ dependence after E.380) and without $f^{xc}$; DFPT screening (§A.3) is static but includes both. Nor is there an electron–hole ladder: $\Pi^{\rm e}$ is the independent-particle bubble, so the theory has no excitons. Replacing $\Pi^{\rm e}$ by the BSE current–current response, with its long-range ($\bG=0$) exchange term removed because that term is the longitudinal photon line of $D$ itself, would give exciton polaritons; exciton–phonon coupling would need phonon lines inside the BSE kernel. Neither is in the manuscript (§B.5).
  • Phonon-assisted optics. Light is now an internal field. The indirect absorption that Giustino treats with a classical field (§A.9) has not been rederived inside EPP.
  • Out-of-plane dipoles in 2D. The 2D results keep only in-plane modes and use a strictly 2D screening model. The ZO modes with $Z^*_{zz}$, and the full sheet propagator with retardation, are left for later.
  • Polaritons beyond the zone centre. The transverse sector of E.380 with $\Pi^{\rm ion}$ contains the full phonon-polariton dispersion, but the manuscript works out only its $q=0$ end point (E.410); the isotropic branches are derived on this page (§B.6, §B.7). Anisotropic crystals, where $\Pi_{jj}$ mixes the L and T sectors off the principal axes, are not treated, so the hyperbolic phonon polaritons of hBN are outside the manuscript as written.

Note on the source

The EPP manuscript is a working draft. The typos and inconsistencies flagged in the grey boxes of each section are collected in §Z.2; none of them changes the conclusions above.

Z.2Appendix · EPP draft and Giustino 2017

Notes on the sources

What turned up when every equation in this primer was checked against the two PDFs: inconsistencies in the EPP draft, a shorter list for Giustino's review, and the conventions that differ between them.

The EPP manuscript is a working draft. Its derivations are written out step by step, which is what made a line-by-line check possible. While building this primer we checked every displayed equation against the PDF and collected the inconsistencies below, so that they can be fixed in the next version. Each item was checked again against the PDF before it went into the table, and items that did not hold up were dropped. Page numbers refer to the PDF. Equation numbers are the manuscript's, written E.n as elsewhere on this page.

Most items are typos, notation or unit bookkeeping. The items marked physics mostly correct an intermediate statement or its justification. None of the items overturns the manuscript's end results: the Dyson equation for the total propagator (E.379–E.380), the electrostatic phonon self-energy (E.452–E.454) and the 2D results (E.471–E.472). Three items do change how a displayed result should be read, or where it applies. E.410 is the $q=0$ point of the upper phonon polariton, not the LO–TO splitting (item 47). The electrostatic Fröhlich vertices on pp. 95 and 98 acquire a factor $e$, which is the "missing $e^2$" the author notes on p. 96 (item 54). The basis phase missing from E.121–E.131 (item 14) does not matter as $q\to0$ but does matter for acoustic modes and at finite $q$ in cells with more than one atom.

EPP manuscript

Kinds: typo a slip in a symbol, label or word; notation a clash or inconsistency of symbols that does not change the physics; units a missing charge or unit-system factor; physics a statement or justification that needs to change; citation a reference, internal or external. The last column links to the primer section where the point is discussed.

Giustino 2017

The review is a refereed and carefully edited article, and the list is shorter and mostly local. Journal page 015003-N is PDF page N. None of them changes the review's conclusions. Several do not propagate at all: the $N_p$ issue is a choice of normalization, Eq. 127 does not enter Eq. 128, the index order in Eq. 100 drops out of Eqs. 104–110, and Fig. 3 illustrates a schematic model.

Eq. 56 has a redundant $\sum_{\bG''}$, and its $\Omega^2$ needs a normalization of $\chi^0_{\bG\bG'}$ that is not stated. $V_\kappa(\bq+\bG)$ in Eq. 43 is not periodic, so the unit-cell transform defined there does not apply. The screening length is $1/k_{\rm TF}$.notation§A.3

Conventions to keep in mind when reading both

  • Units. Giustino is SI throughout ($e^2/4\pi\varepsilon_0=14.40$ eV Å). EPP §3 is SI, and §4 onward is Gaussian. Convert with $e^2/4\pi\varepsilon_0\leftrightarrow e^2$ and $1/\varepsilon_0\leftrightarrow4\pi$. Every displayed equation in this primer says which system it uses (§X.2, §B.2).
  • Born charges. Giustino's $\bZ^*_\kappa$ is dimensionless. EPP's $Z^*$ carries the charge, $Z^*_{\rm EPP}=|e|\,Z^*_{\rm G}$, which hides one factor $e$ whenever the two papers' vertices are compared (§B.1, §X.2).
  • Number versus charge density. EPP's $\rho_{\rm e}=\Psi^\dagger\Psi$ counts electrons, while $\rho_{\rm ion}=-\nabla\cdot\bP$ and $\bj_{\rm e}$ carry charge. A factor $e$ belongs wherever $\rho_{\rm e}$ meets a charge: Gauss's law, the Coulomb energy, continuity with $\bj$ (§B.4, §B.8).
  • Name clashes. $D$ is Giustino's nuclear density correlator, displacement correlator and phonon propagator (G Eqs. 103, 109, 132), next to his dynamical matrix $D^{\rm dm}$; in EPP it is the photon propagator. $\Pi$ is Giustino's phonon self-energy and EPP's photon self-energy $\Pi_{jj}$. $\Omega$ is the unit-cell volume in Giustino; in EPP it is the crystal volume (the cell is $\Omega_{\rm uc}$), the force-constant matrix $\Omega^2$ of §1 and the phonon self-energy $\Omega^{\rm e}$. $\sigma$ is EPP's phonon branch, photon polarization (E.219) and $l/t$ label (E.324), and the conductivity elsewhere. This primer writes Giustino's phonon propagator $\mathcal D$ and his phonon self-energy $\Pi^{\rm ph}$ (§X.2).
  • Two meanings of "retardation". Giustino, following Bardeen and Pines, means frequency-dependent electronic screening, $\epsilon(\bq,\omega)$ in place of $\epsilon(\bq,0)$ (G pp. 4, 12, 18). EPP means the finite speed of light, and its $c\to\infty$ limit is the instantaneous, non-retarded one (§X.1).
  • Time-ordered versus retarded. Both papers mostly write $T=0$ time-ordered propagators with $+i\eta$, which agree with retarded functions only for $\omega\gt0$. Giustino's finite-temperature Fan–Migdal form (Eq. 158) is retarded, so his signs of $\Gamma_{n\bk}$ for electrons and holes hold for the time-ordered Eq. 157 only. The figures in this primer use retarded forms, $\omega^2-\omega_0^2+i\gamma\omega$ (§A.7, §A.8, §B.5).
  • Normalizations. Giustino's $g$ (G Eq. 38) is $N_p$-independent, with $N_p^{-1/2}$ in the Hamiltonian; EPP puts $N^{-1/2}$ inside $g$. Giustino's phonon $\gamma$ is a half width ($\tau^{\rm ph}=(2\gamma)^{-1}$, p. 23), and his $N_F$ is not declared per spin; the heat capacity (Eq. 192) and the Eliashberg formulas (Eqs. 205–210) imply per spin, the Saitta formula with Eq. 145 both spins (Giustino item 11; §A.2, §A.6).

  2. “Theory of the Electron-Phonon-Photon coupling”, 102-page manuscript (draft v2), the source of Part B.
  3. C. Verdi and F. Giustino, “Fröhlich electron-phonon vertex from first principles”, Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 176401 (2015).
  4. J. Sjakste, N. Vast, M. Calandra and F. Mauri, Phys. Rev. B 92, 054307 (2015).
  5. X. Gonze and C. Lee, Phys. Rev. B 55, 10355 (1997): Born charges, dielectric tensors and the nonanalytic term of the dynamical matrix.
  6. S. Baroni, S. de Gironcoli, A. Dal Corso and P. Giannozzi, Rev. Mod. Phys. 73, 515 (2001): density-functional perturbation theory.
  7. L. Hedin, Phys. Rev. 139, A796 (1965); G. Baym, Ann. Phys. (N.Y.) 14, 1 (1961).
  8. J. Bardeen and D. Pines, Phys. Rev. 99, 1140 (1955); H. Fröhlich, Adv. Phys. 3, 325 (1954).
  9. K. Huang, Proc. R. Soc. London A 208, 352 (1951): phonon polaritons; R. H. Lyddane, R. G. Sachs and E. Teller, Phys. Rev. 59, 673 (1941).
  10. S. L. Adler, Phys. Rev. 126, 413 (1962); N. Wiser, Phys. Rev. 129, 62 (1963): microscopic dielectric response.

  13. N. S. Rytova, Proc. MSU Phys. Astron. 3, 30 (1967); L. V. Keldysh, JETP Lett. 29, 658 (1979): screening in thin films.
